title: Microfluidic Production of Mangiferin-Loaded Liposomes Enables Gut–Joint Axis Modulation for Early Osteoarthritis Intervention
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Microfluidic nanomanufacturing provides a controllable and scalable strategy for improving the oral delivery of poorly bioavailable natural compounds. Herein, mangiferin-loaded liposomes (Lip@MG) were fabricated using an in-house-developed continuous microfluidic platform integrated with a high-efficiency micromixer and evaluated as a gut–joint axis-oriented intervention for early knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Compared with the conventional batch method, microfluidic synthesis produced Lip@MG with a more uniform spherical morphology, a clearly defined bilayer structure, and a narrower particle size distribution. By adjusting the flow-rate ratio, Lip@MG with tunable particle sizes from 207.8 to 118.6 nm, reduced polydispersity, and stable negative zeta potentials of up to approximately –35 mV was obtained. In vitro, Lip@MG exhibited favorable cytocompatibility and enhanced chondrocyte viability. Transcriptomic analysis, qRT-PCR, and western blot further indicated that Lip@MG attenuated LPS-induced inflammatory responses in chondrocytes, at least partly by suppressing NF-κB signaling and inhibiting p65 phosphorylation. In an anterior cruciate ligament transection-induced KOA mouse model, oral Lip@MG administration alleviated cartilage degeneration, increased cartilage thickness from 132 to 215 μm, reduced the OARSI score from 2.5 to 1.5, increased subchondral bone mineral density by 27%, and restored colonic barrier integrity, as reflected by a 65% reduction in the colonic histopathological score. Full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing revealed that Lip@MG reshaped KOA-associated gut dysbiosis by partially restoring the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes balance and enriching potentially beneficial taxa. These findings demonstrate that microfluidically manufactured Lip@MG is a promising nutritional nanocarrier for microbiota-centered early KOA intervention through coordinated regulation of intestinal homeostasis and joint degeneration.

title: Atomic Resolution Microscopy Reveals Cluster, Charge Transport, and Diffusion Metrics in Guest:Host Blend Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quantitatively determining the 3D arrangement of guest molecules in a guest:host emissive layer remains a challenge, particularly for beam-sensitive organic materials. By extracting 3D coordinates from depth-sectioned HAADF–STEM stacks of Ir(ppy)2(acac):TCTA and Ir(ppy)3:TCTA vacuum-deposited guest:host blend films, we enable direct access to molecular-scale morphology in beam-sensitive materials. We find that guest aggregation is significantly stronger than expected from random distributions, with the difference diminishing only at high concentrations. Coupling these morphologies to master equation transport modeling reveals that aggregation alters transport pathways and reduces mobility. Additionally, thermal motion of guest molecules between the image frames provides an estimate of molecular diffusion, linking structural and dynamic behavior.

title: A Graphene Oxide-Based Tribo-Piezoelectric Hybrid Sensor for Armed Swimming Action Recognition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Limb movement analysis provides a convenient and effective approach for physiological safety monitoring and motion standardization assessment of personnel working in humid, wading, or underwater environments. However, in wet and wading environments, the existing wearable flexible sensors generally suffer from several limitations such as insufficient sensitivity, rapid performance degradation, and poor environmental stability. In this paper, we propose a corrosion-resistant tribo-piezoelectric hybrid sensor (CRTPHS) primarily composed of an intrinsically corrosion-resistant fluorinated graphene oxide film with a micro-truncated pyramid array structure (MFGOF) and gold-coated polydimethylsiloxane-barium zirconate titanate (PDMS-BZT). The CRTPHS exhibited a sensitivity of up to 1.86 V/N, a response time of 106 ms, a peak power density of 1.98 mW/m2, and stable output performance after 50,000 cycles. In corrosion resistance tests, the CRTPHS retained a sensitivity of 1.27 V/N and excellent underwater sensing capability even after 3 days of seawater immersion. By integrating a lightweight random forest (RF) algorithm, the CRTPHS enabled recognition of five simulated armed-swimming motion states, achieving an average cross-subject accuracy of 99.25% ± 0.07% under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV). This study not only provides a novel fabrication method for developing corrosion-resistant self-powered sensors but also offers a new strategy for intelligent posture recognition in corrosive seawater environments.

title: Control of spin-to-charge conversion by chirality switching of spin texture in a three-dimensional hybrid perovskite
abstract: A strategy to switch the chirality of spin texture in hybrid perovskites, without the aid of an applied electric field, has been established. The switching of spin texture chirality can be used to manipulate the spin-to-charge conversion. The electric current, generated by coherent magnon mediated spin current or photo induced spin current, changes sign during the transition from static to dynamic Rashba effect, which demonstrates its applications in spintronic and magnonic devices.

title: Stacked-Ring Aromaticity Rewires Quantum Interference and Through-Space Transport
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stacking antiaromatic rings does more than switch aromaticity: it rewires how electrons interfere and flow through space. Here, we show that stacked-ring aromaticity (SRA), generated by cofacial coupling of 4nπ antiaromatic molecules, transforms their quantum-transport landscape. Vertical compression converts paratropic monomers into cylindrically delocalized aromatic dimers with continuous interlayer current-density flux and strong through-space electronic coupling. Remarkably, this antiaromatic-to-SRA transition systematically inverts the preferred electrode connectivity: the anchoring topology that favors transport in the monomer becomes the less efficient interlayer pathway in the dimeric configuration, while the alternative connectivity becomes dominant. This behavior arises from the reorganization of destructive quantum-interference features through interlayer orbital coupling. The effect is maximized near d = 2.70 Å, where magnetic reversal, energetic stabilization, and high interlayer transmission converge. This connectivity inversion is rationalized by a minimal Green’s function analysis as a layer-parity effect that changes the phase condition governing quantum interference in opposite-layer transport. Interestingly, the odd-layered stacking remains globally antiaromatic yet preserves efficient transport across the full three-layer stack, showing that the stacking-induced transport network survives the even–odd magnetic reversal. SRA therefore provides a mechanically accessible strategy for reshaping quantum interference and through-space conductance in molecular junctions.

title: Structural Reconstruction of Ternary CuCo2S4 for Boosting Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3RR) represents a promising strategy for sustainable ammonia synthesis while simultaneously addressing nitrate pollution in wastewater. However, the irreversible structural reconstruction commonly observed in catalysts during NO3RR obscures the true active sites and complicates mechanistic understanding. In this study, flower-like CuCo2S4 nanocrystals synthesized via a hot-injection method serve as a model ternary sulfide system to systematically probe reconstruction dynamics and identify active phases under operating conditions. Experimental characterizations reveal that CuCo2S4 gradually evolves into Cu-Co(OH)2/Co9S8 through electrochemical reconstruction. This reconstructed catalyst exhibits excellent NO3RR performance, achieving an average Faradaic efficiency of 97.3%, an ammonia production rate of 363.1 μmol h–1 mg–1, and remarkable cycling stability. In situ FTIR spectra indicate that Cu incorporation promotes the conversion of *NO2 and accelerates subsequent hydrogenation steps. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that Cu doping facilitates *NH3 desorption and optimizes the balance between NO3– adsorption and *NH3 release. This work systematically deciphers the reconstruction pathway of sulfide catalysts during NO3RR, offering fundamental insights into electrocatalyst reconstruction mechanisms and providing a design strategy for high-performance ammonia-production electrocatalysts.

title: Interfacial Kinetic Control Enables Regulated Growth of Functional Metal–Phenolic Network Films
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–phenolic network (MPN) films are of widespread interest because of their potential application in biotechnology, catalysis, and the environment. Their formation typically involves the supramolecular assembly of phenolic ligands and metal ions from solution onto a solid substrate. Such assembly has been conducted exclusively from a single-phase solution, thus limiting spatiotemporal control over coordination and/or the range of precursors that can be used, and thereby restricting the compositional and structural diversity, as well as functionality, of MPN films. Herein, we report a liquid–liquid interfacial assembly (LLIA) approach, which leverages two immiscible phases, to prepare functional MPN films with specific properties. LLIA enables both the kinetic regulation of film growth (a key parameter in designing films with desired properties) and the use of a broader range of building blocks. The assembled MPN films exhibit controlled thickness (∼30–500 nm) and stiffness (∼2–12 GPa) and distinct structural properties (e.g., crystallinity) relative to other methods, which contribute to their conductivity and molecular selectivity (e.g., H2/CO2 separation performance). Functional MPN films with wettability, conductivity, antibacterial, or fluorescence properties are assembled by integrating various functional components (e.g., polymers, nanoparticles, and dyes), as well as inorganic and metal–organic framework films.

title: Topology-Directed Pore Space Compartmentalization and Densification in MOFs Enable Record Trace C3H6 Capture and C2H4 Purification
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Adsorptive separation of C3H6 from C2H4 is of great relevance yet highly challenging to the petrochemical industry, especially for trace C3H6 capture. Here, we constructed two metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), NKU-410 and NKU-411, through pillaring of the kgd- and hxl-topology supermolecular building layers (SBLs) comprised of a novel fluoride-bridging hexanuclear niccolite cluster. In terms of topological net merging and pillaring, a three-dimensional compartmentalization of pore space was implemented, reconstructing the less confined pore space in NKU-410 into a dense array of uniform strongly confined pore cavities in NKU-411. Leveraging the pore confinement effect, NKU-411 impressively attains an ultrahigh C3H6 uptake of 47.5 cm3 g–1 at 298 K and 0.01 bar, together with an appreciable C3H6/C2H4 (1/99, v/v) selectivity of 36.9, placing it among the benchmark MOFs for trace C3H6 capture from C2H4. Dynamic breakthrough experiments demonstrated that NKU-411 shows excellent C2H4 purification and C3H6 recovery performances at ambient conditions over a wide range of separation scenarios with varying feed concentrations and compositions, remarkably affording a record-breaking C2H4 (≥99.999% pure) productivity of 639.4 L kg–1 from C3H6/C2H4 (1/99, v/v) mixture. In-depth mechanistic studies disclosed that the well-tailored pore cavity in NKU-411 represents a “sweet spot” for C3H6 and the dense arrangement of such “sweet spot” maximally optimizes the pore space utilization, providing a new paradigm for boosting the ultralow-pressure gas adsorption capacity and selectivity for MOFs.

title: Set efficiency criteria for access to geological carbon dioxide storage
abstract: Geological CO2 storage sites are critical to achieving climate-relevant carbon sequestration. Efficiency metrics should be used to ensure that limited storage capacity is not used on CO2 from capture projects with high levels of life-cycle carbon emissions.

title: Optimizing systems rather than parts
abstract: Developing and deploying clean technologies to reach net-zero carbon emissions will require more than optimizing individual processes and technologies. System-level thinking is needed to identify trade-offs, handle uncertainty and future scenarios, and support decision-making, as highlighted by articles in a new Collection.

title: Secondary materials in photovoltaics manufacturing
abstract: The use of secondary materials in photovoltaics could reduce resource demand, waste generation and supply-chain risks. This Review benchmarks recycled content use across silicon photovoltaic materials and identifies technical and market barriers to wider adoption.

title: Conductive Composite-Based Wearable Sensors for Sports Science: Intelligent Data Analysis and Emerging Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Wearable sensors enable continuous acquisition of physiological, biochemical, and biomechanical signals during exercise, providing data to support sports performance assessment, training regulation, fatigue monitoring, and rehabilitation interventions. However, signal reliability and multidimensional data analysis under complex motion conditions remain constrained by device functionality. Conductive composites can improve sensor flexibility, interfacial conformability, and signal acquisition performance, while artificial intelligence (AI) enables movement pattern recognition, state assessment, and outcome prediction from complex data. Their integration is advancing wearable systems toward multimodal sensing and intelligent analysis. Guided by application needs in sports, this review summarizes emerging applications of wearable sensing technologies enabled by conductive composites and AI. First, the relevance to sports science and the data characteristics of physiological, biochemical, and biomechanical signals are introduced. The functional characteristics, representative applications, and major limitations of conductive polymer, carbon-based, MXene, and hydrogel composites are then summarized. Regarding algorithms, the fundamental principles of supervised learning, unsupervised learning, deep learning (DL), and large language models (LLMs) are discussed, with comparisons of their capabilities in feature extraction, temporal modeling, and multisource data analysis, as well as their input data requirements. On this basis, advances in the application of these systems to sports performance and sport-specific movement monitoring, exercise-induced fatigue monitoring and assessment, sports injury identification and evaluation, and intelligent monitoring of sports rehabilitation are reviewed followed by a discussion of current challenges and future directions. Through the coordinated integration of material design, signal acquisition, and intelligent analysis, wearable systems are expected to enable continuous, reliable, and individualized assessment of exercise-related states, with further applications in real-time feedback, risk alerts, and training decision support, providing a technological foundation for scientifically informed training, sports rehabilitation, and individual health management.

title: Organic Upconversion Devices for NIR–II Biometric Sensing and Imaging Enabled by an Isomerically Engineered Narrow-Bandgap Quinoidal Polymer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The limited availability of organic donor materials absorbing beyond 1000 nm fundamentally limits the development of solution-processed photodetectors and upconversion devices (UCDs) in the second near-infrared (NIR-II) window. Herein, we report DPP-TbT, a narrow-bandgap alternating copolymer realized through isomeric engineering of the thiophene backbone. By employing a thieno[3,4-b]thiophene (TbT) quinoidal donor fused to a diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) acceptor, the absorption onset is extended to ∼1300 nm, enabling intrinsic NIR-II photon harvesting. When blended with the benchmark non-fullerene acceptor Y6 to form bulk-heterojunction photodetectors, the DPP-TbT:Y6 system achieves a specific detectivity exceeding 1011 Jones at 1064 nm with a linear dynamic range (LDR) of 68 dB. Monolithic integration of this photodetector with a quantum-dot light-emitting diode further yields a UCD that directly transduces 1064 nm excitation into visible emission with a turn-on voltage of ∼2 V, a luminance of 3741 cd m–2, and a luminance-LDR of 60 dB. We further demonstrate real-time heart-rate monitoring via photoplethysmography, high-resolution biological imaging (5080 ppi), and visualization of hidden information through a 1000 nm long-pass filter. This work establishes isomeric engineering as a rational strategy for accessing ultra-narrow bandgaps and advancing low-cost, wearable NIR-II visualization and biometric sensing systems.

title: Interface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Sensor Enabled by Hairy-Particle-Analyte Noncovalent Coupling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Raman enhancement in practical sensing is dominated by surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS), where signal amplification relies on localized plasmonic hotspots but is often limited by inefficient analyte access. Conventional SERS platforms further require multistep assembly on rigid substrates, exhibit ligand-limited stability associated with thiol-metal coordination, and rely on time-consuming off-site detection (>12 h), limiting reproducibility and practical deployment. Here, we develop an interface-engineered SERS strategy, referred to as interface-enhanced Raman scattering (IERS), in which a polymer-grafted plasmonic interface regulates analyte enrichment and access to electromagnetic hotspots. Diblock copolymer-grafted gold nanoparticles form “hairy” particles, in which an N-heterocyclic carbene-functionalized block drives spontaneous interparticle hotspot formation, while a poly(acrylic acid) block promotes noncovalent analyte enrichment and nanoconfinement. This interfacial nanoconfinement suppresses fluorescence and is consistent with an additional charge-transfer contribution. As a result, IERS enables rapid fabrication via simple mixing of “hairy” particles in soft hydrogels, robust stability through multidentate NHC coordination, and fast on-site detection (<15 min). The sensor achieves broadband trace detection, strong tolerance to fluorescent interference, and excellent batch-to-batch reproducibility. The conformal sensing capability was further demonstrated by proof-of-concept detection of prothioconazole on a pesticide-spiked curved apple surface.

title: High-Performance Planar Ni/Si Photothermoelectric Photodetectors Enabled by MnO2 Nanosheets
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photodetectors are the key component of modern communication systems, surveillance applications, robotics, and scientific research. The photothermoelectric effect offers opportunity to fabricate broadband and self-driven photodetectors utilizing thermally energized charge carriers. Unfortunately, photothermoelectric photodetectors are facing the challenge of large dark current, leading to low detectivity, linear dynamic range, and on–off ratio. Herein, we design a planar Ni/n-Si device structure with the help of a monolayer of MnO2 nanosheets for contact engineering. The demonstrated device shows a broadband detection range from 200 nm to MIR with an external quantum efficiency of 263.6%, a photoresponsivity of 455.1 mA W–1, a detectivity of ∼7.25 × 1012 Jones, and an on–off ratio of ∼103 at 0 V. Additionally, the device shows an unprecedented bias-assisted photoresponsivity and external quantum efficiency of 21.56 A W–1 and 13,363%, respectively, with 200 nm illumination at –10 V. The nanosheet-based contact engineering provides a powerful strategy to fabricate self-powered photodetectors with high photoresponsivity, external quantum efficiency, and broadband detection from the solar blind region to the MIR spectrum.

title: An Asynchronous Neuromorphic Architecture for Wearable EEG Emotion Recognition
abstract: Neural activity associated with emotion is event-driven and temporally sparse, whereas electroencephalography (EEG) is acquired as a continuous signal rather than a usable event stream. Conventional synchronous hardware processes all time steps densely, increasing energy costs during prolonged wearable monitoring. We propose an asynchronous neuromorphic architecture in which a dynamic adaptive spiking neural network converts features derived from EEG into sparse spike events. The model combines a depthwise separable gating module, division-free time-to-first-spike encoding, and adaptive temporal window regulation. The resulting events drive a globally asynchronous locally synchronous (GALS) accelerator that activates data movement and computation only for valid events, reducing switching during idle periods. DA-SNN outperforms lightweight models on SEED, SEED-IV, SEED-V, DEAP, and DREAMER. The accelerator completes inference on a preprocessed EEG tensor in 18 μs, with total power consumption of 148 mW and energy consumption of 2.66 μJ per inference.

title: Thermochemical adsorption at high overpotentials limits molecular CO-to-methanol electroreduction
abstract: Electrocatalysis modulates interfacial charge-transfer kinetics through potential control. However, it remains unclear how thermochemical steps, such as adsorption, dictate these overall kinetics. Here we determine CO-reduction limiting currents by measuring CO-oxidation limiting currents, allowing mass-transport effects to be deconvoluted from the CO-reduction kinetics. Using CO-to-methanol conversion on molecular catalysts as a model system, we show that while the reaction rate is limited by an electrochemical step at low overpotentials, the thermochemical CO adsorption step becomes rate limiting at high overpotentials. Cation-dependent variations in CO adsorption energies and activation energies align with the Brønsted-Evans-Polanyi principle, establishing CO adsorption energy as a robust kinetic descriptor. We further demonstrate that cobalt phthalocyanine supported on carbon nanotubes enables appreciable CO-to-methanol conversion due to its enhanced CO adsorption compared to other metal phthalocyanines. Ultimately, these findings illuminate an inherent thermochemical constraint on electrolysis and provide a kinetic framework to identify when such limitations become rate determining.

title: Disentanglement of interfacial electric fields and electrochemical potential gradients reveals a multidimensional kinetic landscape
abstract:
Abstract
                  Electrochemical reactions occur at solid–liquid interfaces, where the applied electrochemical potential gradient can act as thermodynamic driving force but can also induce interfacial polarization. A key question has long been how local changes in the chemical potentials of the electrons and the associated excess charge and electric fields impact catalyst kinetics. Here we combine temperature-dependent current transients from oxidative CO stripping with a CO coverage-dependent potential of zero total charge and Raman spectroscopy. We observe a reduction of the activation energy with increasing driving force. By contrast, increasing the distance between the applied potential and the potential of zero total charge results in an increase in the apparent activation energy, which we ascribe to an electric field effect in the double layer. More generally, the results demonstrate how interfacial changes in the chemical potentials give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape, in which single-descriptor kinetics fail to capture the nature of the overpotential.

title: Organic Spacer Cation Engineering Enhances the Electroluminescence of Full-Color PeLEDs
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites have great potential in pure-blue perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs). Nevertheless, disordered multi-n phase distribution gives rise to inhomogeneous quantum confinement, accompanied by high charge-transport barriers, which severely restrict the performance of pure-blue devices. This paper proposes a universal dual-functional modification strategy, which achieves efficient pure-blue PeLEDs by partially replacing phenethylammonium bromide (PEABr) with 2-methoxyethylammonium bromide (MOAmBr). Due to the smaller steric hindrance of MOAmBr and its strong interaction with the perovskite framework, it can effectively reduce the interlayer spacing of quasi-2D perovskites and regulate the distribution of phases, thereby enhancing quantum confinement and achieving a blueshift and high-purity electroluminescence (EL). At the same time, MOAmBr reduces the carrier injection barrier, improves charge migration, and inhibits internal recombination losses of the device. The optimized pure-blue PeLED achieves a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 6.8% at 469 nm. Additionally, this universal strategy is successfully applied to green and red PeLEDs, achieving significant EQE values of 21.69 and 17.29% at 506 and 660 nm, respectively. This work provides a simple and versatile cation engineering method for constructing high-performance full-spectrum quasi-2D PeLEDs.

title: Polarized 3D Bicontinuous bcu Covalent Organic Frameworks with Accessible Octa-Sites for High-Efficiency Oxygen Electrocatalysis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional (3D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are potential metal-free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) due to their inherent porosity and potential for fully exposed active sites. However, their practical application is severely hindered by inefficient electron transport along the extended framework and the resultant high kinetic barriers. Herein, we report a series of highly crystalline and non-interpenetrated 8-connected body-centered cubic (bcu) COFs featuring eight unstacked catalytic nodes per unit cell for ORR. By integrating redox-active azobenzene (Azo) units into the linkages, we successfully bridge the gap between electronic conductivity and catalytic activity. The incorporated Azo moieties not only narrow the bandgap but also serve as electron reservoirs, facilitating rapid electron shuttling to the imine-based active sites. Consequently, the optimal DZPy-COF achieves a remarkable half-wave potential of 0.77 V under alkaline conditions, coupled with a high turnover frequency (0.03 s–1) and enhanced capacitance (13.7 mF cm–2). Theoretical calculations reveal that the Azo units polarize the framework, lowering the energy barrier for intermediate formation, which is the rate-determining step in conventional 3D COFs. This work underscores the efficacy of leveraging high-valency topologies combined with redox-active linkages to overcome electron transport limitations in crystalline porous catalysts.

title: Sequence-Engineered Multifunctional Peptide Nanozyme Gel for Catalytic Microenvironment Regulation in Diabetic Infected Wounds
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent infection, redox imbalance, and dysregulated enzymatic activity, yet current biomaterials largely function as passive dressings, with limited capacity to actively intervene in the stalled healing cascade. Here, we report a sequence-programmed peptide nanozyme that encodes multiple enzyme-mimetic activities within a single supramolecular framework for adaptive microenvironment regulation. By mimicking the coordination motifs of natural hydrolases and superoxide dismutase, a de novo peptide sequence, C7-RD(S)HHEEH, was rationally engineered to encode integrated nitrogen/oxygen metal-binding sites. The incorporation of a side-chain–modified serine enhances coordination adaptability, while glutamate residues facilitate catalytic functionality. Upon Cu2+ coordination, the peptide self-assembles into a nanozyme exhibiting hydrolase (HYD)-, oxidase (OXD)-, peroxidase (POD)-, and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activities within a unified framework, thereby enabling coordinated regulation of enzymatic debridement, antibacterial defense, and redox homeostasis. Incorporated into a sprayable gelatin hydrogel, the nanozyme provides conformal wound coverage while maintaining excellent biocompatibility and sustained catalytic functionality. In a diabetic bacteria-infected wound model, the nanozyme gel significantly accelerates wound closure, enhances angiogenesis and collagen deposition, and restores tissue regeneration. Our work demonstrates that rational peptide sequence design can encode complex, multimodal catalysis into synthetic nanozymes, offering a programmable approach for active regulation of pathological microenvironments in chronic wound therapy.

title: Ag Nanowire/Mo2CTx Transparent Electrodes with Chemically Tunable Work Function for Near- and Shortwave-Infrared Photodetectors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transparent electrodes that simultaneously combine low sheet resistance, broadband infrared transparency, and tunable interfacial energetics are critically needed for emerging infrared optoelectronics, yet are rarely achieved within a single solution-processable architecture. Here, we report a hybrid transparent electrode composed of a percolative Ag nanowire network overcoated with Mo2CTx MXene nanosheets (Ag/MX). In this architecture, Ag nanowires provide an efficient conductive scaffold, while the Mo2CTx overlayer bridges interwire junctions, smooths the surface, and governs the device-facing interfacial electronic structure. The resulting electrodes exhibit a low sheet resistance of 18.84 Ω/sq together with a transmittance of 82% at 1550 nm and an average transmittance of 80.84% over 1500–2500 nm. More importantly, two distinct surface-modification routes enable chemically tunable work-function states: polyethyleneimine lowers the work function through interfacial dipole formation, whereas UV/Ozone treatment raises it through oxygen-enriched surface termination and mild surface oxidation of the Mo2CTx overlayer. These chemically distinct low and high work function states allow the common AgNW/Mo2CTx (Ag/MX) electrode architecture to meet different carrier-selective requirements in quantum dot short-wave-infrared and organic near-infrared photodetectors. This work establishes a chemically tunable transparent-electrode platform for cross-material infrared photodetection and provides a strategy for integrating infrared transparency, electrical transport, and carrier-selective interfacial energetics within a common electrode architecture.

title: Bismuth electron buffering stabilizes alkaline hydrogen evolution under intermittent operation
abstract: A bismuth overlayer reversibly buffers oxidative charge to protect NiCo cathodes. It suppresses metal dissolution and sustains alkaline hydrogen evolution during startup–shutdown and reverse-current cycling under industrially relevant conditions.

title: Reconstructing the single-cell spatiotemporal dynamics of glioblastoma invasion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Glioblastoma invasion into healthy brain tissue remains a major barrier to effective treatment, but the dynamic single-cell behaviors underlying this process remain difficult to measure across patient models. Here, we introduce GlioTrace, an ex vivo imaging and computational framework for real-time tracking of glioblastoma invasion in patient-derived xenograft brain slices. Combining whole-specimen confocal microscopy with machine learning-based morphology classification and probabilistic modeling of state transitions, GlioTrace reconstructs how tumor cells switch between invasion phenotypes and how these dynamics are shaped by local tissue context and therapy. Across six patient-derived models, GlioTrace reveals that invasion plasticity is patient-specific, spatially organized, and modulated by vascular proximity and microglial interaction. Targeted therapies selectively alter phenotype composition and transition probabilities, whereas standard-of-care treatment enriches a highly motile, transition-connected branching state consistent with a treatment-tolerant invasive phenotype. Thus, GlioTrace makes glioblastoma invasion a measurable dynamic process for comparing patient-specific treatment responses in living brain tissue.

title: ‘A perfect scientist, a perfect mum’: researchers mourn two biologists’ deaths in Spanish train crash
abstract: Scientists pay tribute to Marta Shahbazi Alonso and Tamara González Costa who died on their way to a developmental-biology meeting.

title: Maternal mental health liveability shaped by composite residential environmental profiles
abstract: Women are a vulnerable population for mental illnesses, with the perinatal period representing a particularly high-risk susceptible window. Whereas maternal mental health research often narrowly focused on postpartum depression, psychological disturbances during pregnancy received insufficient attention. Here we analyzed a Chinese nationwide 13-year maternity cohort involving 216,442 pregnant women, revealing that the prevalence of prenatal mental distress symptoms peaked at 31.8%. We identified a broad spectrum of risk determinants, spanning socioeconomic disadvantages, behavioral vulnerabilities, medical histories and suboptimal residential environmental exposures. We estimated that 1.61 (95% uncertainty interval: 1.35–1.88) million prenatal mental distress symptoms were attributable to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and heatwave exposure, while green spaces prevented 791.7 (95% uncertainty interval: 648.1–948.9) thousand cases. We further delineated multiple pathways through which urban greening confers mental well-being benefits, including attenuation of pollution-associated stress, reduction of heatwave occurrence, encouragement of outdoor physical activity and intrinsic mental restoration. Our study ultimately provides policy-oriented evidence to inform fertility-supportive and health-promoting urban planning, echoing China’s ‘three-child policy’ and ‘Healthy China 2030’ blueprint. In a cohort of 216,000+ pregnant women across China, air pollution and heat were linked to higher risks of prenatal mental distress, while nearby green space was protective. Urban greening could support maternal mental health and healthier cities.

title: ATP-dependent dimerization of BrxC coordinates BrxBCZ assembly for phage exclusion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bacteriophage Exclusion (BREX) systems protect bacterial genomes via sequence-specific DNA methylation while blocking phage replication through a poorly understood “restriction-without-cleavage” mechanism. Here, we present cryo-EM structures and functional characterization of the core BREX machinery from Escherichia coli. We determined the structures of the ATPase BrxC in its monomeric state and two ATPγS-bound dimeric conformations, showing that ATP binding, not hydrolysis, triggers dimerization. The conserved Arg328 couples dimer formation to ATP hydrolysis and is required for both phage restriction and host methylation; the R328A mutant supports assembly but abolishes defense. We further resolved the BrxBCZ ternary complex, revealing BrxB as a central scaffold bridging the BrxC dimer and BrxZ without direct BrxC–BrxZ contact. Biochemical assays show that BrxZ is a dual-function enzyme with alkaline phosphatase and metal-dependent nuclease activities. Thus, ATP drives BrxC assembly and inhibits BrxZ activities. Disruption of the BrxB–BrxC interface or the BrxC ATPase cycle selectively eliminates restriction while preserving methylation, establishing BrxBCZ as a restriction-specific structural core. Collectively, these findings delineate the structural basis for ATP-dependent coordination of BREX, revealing how energy metabolism is integrated into bacterial innate immunity.

title: Trifunctional zirconium catalysis-enabled triple modular synthesis
abstract: While zirconium catalysis has been predominantly confined to Lewis acid and redox applications in homogeneous synthesis, its potential in photocatalysis—particularly in C–H activation—remains largely unexplored. Here, with the demonstration of photoinduced inner-sphere α-homolysis (ligand-to-metal charge transfer) in zirconium catalysis, we report a trifunctional zirconium catalytic system synergistically integrating photochemical, Lewis acid and redox catalysis for triple modular synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles, rendering structurally diverse benzylamines (up to 98% yield) and their deuterated analogues under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies validate a multifunctional catalytic cycle combining ligand-to-metal charge transfer-initiated radical chemistry with a ZrIV-mediated carbocation pathway. The protocol’s synthetic power is showcased through late-stage diversification of bioactive compounds, streamlined drug analogue synthesis, direct valorization of gaseous alkanes and gram-scale production with 100% atom economy. Zirconium catalysis has remained largely confined to Lewis acid and redox chemistry, with only isolated examples of photocatalytic C–H activation. Now trifunctional zirconium catalysis enables modular benzylamine synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles by integrating photochemical, redox and Lewis acid reactivity.

title: A distinct class of conjugative megaplasmids is associated with prophages in distantly related bacterial lineages
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Closely related prophages have been found in phylogenetically distant bacteria in the human gut, despite limited evidence of productive phage infections across broad host ranges. It remains enigmatic how the wide distribution of prophages could emerge. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized association between a distinct group of conjugative megaplasmids and prophage genomes. We describe two related but diverged groups of conjugative megaplasmids (>300 kilobases) in the human gut microbiome, which we named Hodors. Hodors encode conserved replication, partitioning, and type IV secretion systems, along with a complex surface-associated gene module. A subset of Hodors harbors complete, intact prophage genomes, and closely related prophages (≥95% nucleotide identity) were detected across phylogenetically distant lineages within the bacterial phylum Bacillota, including both Bacilli and Clostridia. We detected signatures consistent with extracellular particle formation and transcriptional activity of Hodor-associated prophages. Our findings suggest that conjugative megaplasmids could contribute to the movement of related prophage genomes between distantly related bacteria, potentially explaining the widespread occurrence of closely related prophages in phylogenetically distant gut bacteria and the apparent uncoupling between lysogenic and infective host ranges.

title: Process-intrinsic cellular network for sustained strength–ductility across temperatures in a 3D-printed multi-principal-element alloy
abstract: Laser-based additive manufacturing (LAM) provides a transformative route for fabricating Cr-Fe-Co-Ni-Al-Ti-based multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs). These alloys typically rely on L12 precipitate strengthening and thus require post-processing; however, such treatments rarely ensure stable mechanical performance over a wide temperature range. Here we designed a (CrFeCo)48Ni34Al7Ti5V5Ta1 MPEA with a self-assembled body-centred cubic/L21 precipitate cellular network formed intrinsically during LAM. Slip transfer and back-stress hardening across Kurdjumov-Sachs and Nishiyama-Wassermann interfaces and a weakly temperature-dependent stacking fault energy stabilize the dislocation-mediated deformation from 77 to 873 K. Consequently, the MPEA maintains a yield strength above 1 GPa and a uniform elongation of approximately 20% over a wide temperature range, indicating relatively stable tensile performance. This process-intrinsic pathway circumvents the need for post-treatment and reveals interface-mediated plasticity mechanisms. Our findings demonstrate that interface coherency engineering provides a foundation for designing strong yet ductile alloys with reduced temperature sensitivity via LAM.

title: Spin currents in polariton waveguides driven by bright and dark excitons
abstract: The optical spin Hall effect enables the spatial separation of four domains of circularly polarized light from a linearly polarized source through photonic spin-orbit coupling, which arises from non-degenerate transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic modes. This mechanism is ineffective for incoherent photoluminescence. In transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers, bright excitons possess in-plane electric dipoles and strong oscillator strengths, whereas dark excitons have out-of-plane dipoles. Here, by embedding WS2 monolayers in waveguide microcavities, we demonstrate strong coupling between bright excitons and photonic modes, forming exciton-polaritons. Under non-resonant pumping, dark excitons become strongly populated and feed both transverse-magnetic- and transverse-electric-like exciton-polariton modes, each with an out-of-plane electric-field component. We observe the optical spin Hall effect in waveguide polaritons, leading to the formation of eight polarization domains and spin-polarized polariton currents propagating up to 92 ± 1 μm at room temperature. These results establish transition metal dichalcogenide-based polaritonic waveguides as a promising platform for room-temperature spin-optoelectronic devices.

title: Breaking symmetry in nanoparticle superlattices via spontaneous valency
abstract: Nanoparticle superlattices enable programmable material structure through ligand-mediated interactions, but attractive ligand interactions typically limit assembly to densely packed lattices that maximize nearest-neighbour bonding. Intentionally programmed directional bonding and valency are therefore typically assumed to require particle-level anisotropy in shape or surface patterning. Here, using assemblies of flexible, electrostatically active isotropic nanoparticles, we show that valency need not be encoded by particle geometry, but can instead emerge spontaneously during assembly. When ligand coronas are sufficiently deformable, ligands reconfigure to align along interparticle interfaces, generating an effective valency. Using a combination of experiment and simulation, we show that increasing ligand deformability lowers lattice coordination numbers, and identify design considerations for assembling isotropic building blocks into lattices with lower coordination, packing density and symmetry than would be predicted from hard-sphere packing. The work presented here therefore establishes ligand flexibility as a design parameter for programming coordination in nanoparticle assembly.

title: Enhancing salivary gland siRNA activity through transgenic Dicer-2 overexpression restricts arbovirus transmission in Aedes aegypti
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mosquito Aedes aegypti is the primary vector for arboviruses that are pathogenic to humans, including dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses. Following a blood meal, arboviruses initially infect the midgut, disseminate systemically to the carcass, and eventually reach the salivary glands for transmission. Here, we investigate tissue-specific small interfering RNA (siRNA) activity and test whether enhancing this pathway can restrict arbovirus infection. Our results show that salivary glands are less refractory to arboviral infection relative to the carcass, with low expression patterns of siRNA pathway genes. Transgenic overexpression of Dicer-2, a key component of the siRNA pathway, in salivary glands leads to a significant decrease in orthoflavivirus and alphavirus replication. DENV4 small RNA sequencing reveals altered viral RNA processing and increased levels of 21-nt virus-derived siRNAs. Conversely, Dicer-2 overexpression in the fat body, a major carcass tissue, only moderately suppresses dengue and Mayaro virus infection. Notably, simultaneous overexpression of Dicer-2 in both midguts and salivary glands produces the strongest reduction in viral load in saliva, indicating reduced transmission potential. These findings reveal tissue-specific differences in antiviral pathway activity and demonstrate that targeted enhancement of salivary gland antiviral defense can restrict arbovirus transmission.

title: TH-positive pulmonary nerve fiber-epithelial interaction promotes adipose thermogenesis in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cold exposure activates sympathetic neurons in adipose tissue to maintain thermal homeostasis. However, whether sympathetic activation in non-adipose tissues contributes to cross-organ regulation of adipose thermogenesis remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate the activation of TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers (TPNFs) by cold exposure, which further promotes adipose thermogenesis. Specifically, cold exposure activates TPNFs that innervate bronchial Club cells in the lung and leads to a reduction in Secretoglobin family 3A member 1 (SCGB3A1) expression via Adrenergic Receptor β2 (ADRB2). SCGB3A1, a Club cell-specific secretory factor, binds the choline transporter SLC44A2 on adipocytes to restrict choline uptake and impair thermogenic activation. Meanwhile, TPNFs activation induces NGF secretion from Club cells, which in turn strengthens TPNFs innervation of Club cells in a feedforward loop. Importantly, the stimulation of this mechanism via tracheal infusion of the ADRB2 agonist norepinephrine (NE) enhances thermogenesis in mice.

title: Genome-anchored foundation model embeddings improve molecular prediction from histology images
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Precision oncology requires accurate molecular insights, yet obtaining these directly from genomics is costly and time-consuming for broad clinical use. Predicting complex molecular features and patient prognosis directly from routine whole-slide images (WSIs) remains a major challenge for current deep learning methods. Here we introduce PathLUPI, which uses transcriptomic privileged information during training to extract genome-anchored histological embeddings, enabling effective molecular prediction using only WSIs at inference. Through extensive evaluation across 49 molecular oncology tasks using 11,361 cases from 20 cohorts, PathLUPI demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional methods trained solely on WSIs. Crucially, it achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of at least 0.80 across 18 biomarker prediction and molecular subtyping tasks, and a concordance index of at least 0.70 across survival cohorts spanning five major cancer types. Moreover, PathLUPI embeddings reveal distinct cellular morphological signatures associated with specific genotypes, whose spatial fidelity is substantiated in representative high-resolution spatial transcriptomics samples. By effectively encoding molecular context to refine WSI representations, PathLUPI offers a strategy to bridge molecular insights with routine pathology workflows for wider clinical application.

title: Human subthalamic neurons track speech features and couple with auditory cortex during preparatory listening
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The basal ganglia-thalamocortical loop is widely implicated in speech production, yet its role during listening remains underexplored. Here, using a listen-and-repeat syllable-triplet task during deep brain stimulation implantation, we show that human subthalamic nucleus (STN) single‑unit activity is modulated during auditory presentation, and that a subset of neurons encodes phonetic (consonant and vowel) and position features prior to overt speech onset. Using intraoperative microelectrode recordings, across 205 units, ~39% of units changed firing rate during listening. Within these, auditory-syllable units carried phonetic and/or position information, primarily in units also modulated during speech. Auditory presentation also elicited beta‑band desynchronization in STN local field potential (LFP) and revealed frequency‑specific spike‑phase coupling (SPC) with cortex: auditory‑specific units coupled predominantly with superior temporal gyrus (STG) in alpha, whereas units modulated during both auditory and speech epochs preferentially coupled with sensorimotor regions in beta. Together, these results indicate that auditory inputs can rapidly modulate human STN activity during a listen-and-repeat task, support a role for the STN in auditory-motor integration, and indicate frequency‑specific routing within human cortical-subcortical loops from listening to subsequent speech production.

title: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: β-thalassemia is an extensively studied monogenic disorder, yet the basis of its striking phenotypic diversity remains unresolved. Here we present the 1000 β-Thalassemia Genomes Project (KbTGP), providing the first comprehensive atlas of 1,429 Chinese genomes (1,020 probands and 409 unaffected parents, 61.63× coverage) linked to 77 clinical traits. We identify 11 independent phenotype-associated loci in probands, and 15 additional loci by integrating 2,746 ethnically matched controls from the NyuWa Project and the 1000 Genomes Project. Functional experiments further highlight non-coding regions at 17p13.3 and the autophagy-related gene PIK3C3 as modulators of thalassemic phenotypes. Loss-of-function structural variants are enriched in hemoglobinopathy-related genes, and structural variants in TF and SLC25A37 are significantly associated with iron metabolism and fetal hemoglobin, respectively. Notably, de novo structural variants and clonal hematopoiesis mutations are enriched in severe cases. These findings collectively establish a phenome-genome resource that delineates the genetic architecture of β-thalassemia, offering candidate targets for precision therapies and laying the groundwork for future research into dissecting the Mendelian disease variability.

title: Anterior cingulate neurons perform parallel processing of fixated and peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We use our eyes to evaluate objects around us. Models of economic choice emphasise the impact of sequential fixation on valuation and choice, with prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) encoding values of fixated items. Yet whether these regions also evaluate non-fixated peripheral information to guide choice remains unknown. Here we show that in a decision-making task involving four simultaneously presented cues, rhesus macaques use peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice, and that ACC neurons encode this peripheral information. This served two distinct purposes: subjects were more likely to fixate valuable peripheral cues, and more likely to choose valuable options whose cues were never even fixated. ACC, orbitofrontal cortex, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and ventromedial prefrontal cortex neurons all encoded cue value as they were fixated. ACC was unique, however, in also conducting parallel processing of peripheral cues, including cues never fixated, to guide information sampling and choice.

title: Microglia-dependent PDGFB regulation of neuronal KCND2 in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus determines propofol anesthesia induction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying anesthetic-induced unconsciousness remains a central question in both anesthesia research and neuroscience. However, the role of non-neuronal components in modulating anesthetic sensitivity is poorly understood. In this study, we identify a microglia-dependent platelet-derived growth factor subunit B (PDGFB) signaling pathway that modulates propofol anesthesia sensitivity and contributes to the induction of anesthesia in mice. We demonstrate that PDGFB signaling regulates the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 2 (KCND2) in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) in mice, thereby orchestrating the excitability of PVN glutamatergic neurons (PVNGlu) and the activity of their projections to lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons (LHGlu). Microglia deprivation induces PDGFB deficiency and downregulates KCND2, resulting in PVN hyperexcitability and hyperactivation of the PVN → LH arousal circuit, which contributes to resistance to anesthesia induction in mice. Our findings identified non-neuronal molecular mechanism that governs anesthetic sensitivity, complementing the classical γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor-centric model and providing insights into the regulation of anesthesia induction.

title: Building a pre-trained model for single-cell multi-omics analysis beyond highly variable feature selection
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Single-cell multi-omics technologies enable simultaneous measurement of transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic modalities in individual cells, offering a unique opportunity to dissect cellular identity and regulation. The heterogeneity of multi-omics data, together with the wide range of downstream analytical tasks, underscores the need for a versatile computational framework for integrative analysis. However, current multi-omics analysis approaches typically rely on task-specific training and highly variable feature selection, which can hinder effective knowledge transfer across datasets and discard biologically informative signals. Here, we present scPMMI, a pre-trained multimodal model for integrative analysis of single-cell multi-omics data. By grouping features into patches according to genomic coordinates, scPMMI processes tens of thousands of features per cell with reduced reliance on prior feature selection, thereby preserving more complete biological information. Our results demonstrate that scPMMI learns biologically coherent cell representations by jointly modeling multi-omics data. Through further transfer learning, the model can be readily adapted to achieve superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including multi-omics integration, cell type annotation, protein abundance prediction, transcriptomic enhancement, and trajectory reconstruction.

title: A multivalent OMV vaccine induces broad protection against major Klebsiella pneumoniae disease-causing serotypes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The antigenic diversity of Klebsiella pneumoniae surface polysaccharides, O- and K-antigen, represents a significant challenge for developing broadly-acting vaccines. Here we report the development of Kp-OMV4, a multivalent outer membrane vesicle (OMV) vaccine incorporating the four predominant K. pneumoniae O-antigen serotypes responsible for most invasive disease worldwide. Kp-OMV4 elicits robust humoral and cellular immune responses, generating high-titer antibodies against both surface polysaccharides and conserved outer membrane proteins. Vaccine-induced antibodies display complement-mediated bactericidal activity against hypervirulent and multidrug-resistant clinical strains. In a murine sepsis model, immunization confers protection against lethal challenge and significantly reduces post-infection bacterial burden. Importantly, immune sera broadly recognize diverse clinical isolates, including strains expressing O- and K-antigen serotypes not included in the vaccine, supporting potential for broad strain coverage. This study indicates that the multicomponent nature of OMVs can be leveraged to overcome bacterial antigenic diversity and enable the development of vaccines with broad strain coverage.

title: Ketogenic diet stimulates tumor cGAS-Sting pathway and attenuates systemic inflammation via Flavonifractor plautii derived uridine
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cancer progression is frequently accompanied by systemic inflammation and host-wide disturbances, including neuroinflammation-associated cognitive impairment, yet interventions that simultaneously target tumor growth and host dysfunction remain limited. Here we show that a ketogenic diet suppresses tumor growth while improving emotional and cognitive deficits in tumor-bearing mice. The diet elevates circulating and intratumoral uridine and enriches Flavonifractor plautii, a gut bacterium that contributes to host uridine availability. In tumor cells and patient-derived organoids, uridine cooperates with β-hydroxybutyrate to promote cytosolic DNA accumulation and activate cGAS–Sting signaling, consistent with enhanced antitumor immune activity. In parallel, ketogenic diet, uridine supplementation and F. plautii transplantation reduce systemic and hippocampal inflammatory readouts and improve neurobehavioral phenotypes. These findings identify a diet–microbiota–metabolite axis that links ketogenic metabolism to tumor immune signaling and reduced peripheral-to-brain inflammation in preclinical cancer models.

title: Single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy revealed by gastric cancer Perturb-seq
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. To study how gastric cancer molecular phenotypes are regulated by cell-intrinsic genetic alterations interacting with cell-extrinsic therapeutic pressures, we performed direct capture Perturb-seq to interrogate >200 gastric cancer-related genes against 4 distinct epigenetic therapies in normal gastric and gastric cancer lines. We identify 17.7 million pharmocogenomic expression interactions in 625,866 cells representing baseline and post-therapeutic molecular phenotypes. This single-cell pharmacogenomic compendium confirms previously known gene-driven molecular phenotypes, elucidating both poorly characterized genes and gene dosage-molecular phenotype relationships. Molecular phenotypes in post-therapeutic surviving cells capture perturbation-associated pathways associated with drug resistance (epithelial–mesenchymal transition, cell cycle alterations, metabolic reprogramming). Mapping of in vitro molecular phenotypes to primary human gastric cancers uncovers prognostic and spatial variability. Comparative analysis of gene perturbations across therapies and lines reveals both conserved and context-specific molecular alterations. Our results provide a community resource for exploring how Perturb-seq molecular phenotypes are influenced by context dependencies across different drug exposures and cell line backgrounds.

title: Southeast Asian voices on climate change
abstract: Responding to the increasing risks of climate change in Southeast Asia requires research and effective action that considers the unique challenges of the region. In this Viewpoint, researchers and practitioners from the region share their views on the progress made in understanding and responding to climate change.

title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. This enzyme acts on a broad range of N-glycan structures but shows a marked preference for N-glycans attached to glycopeptides rather than to denatured or native proteins, highlighting a specialized route for N-glycan acquisition in infant-associated Bifidobacterium species. Structures of the apo enzyme, an unliganded E236Q mutant, and a D107N–E236Q complex with a G2-peptide reveal a canonical two-β-sandwich PNGase core plus an additional ten-strand β-sheet cradle and are the first structures of this superfamily. Comparison of these states, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, indicates that glycopeptide binding is coupled to β-sheet cradle-loop movements that close against β-sandwich 1 over the peptide C terminus. The complex defines recognition of the two core GlcNAc residues and the central mannose, reveals that peptide contacts are concentrated around the +2 Thr residue of the NXT sequon, and positions the scissile amide at the active site. These findings, together with mutational and computational analyses, provide a structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference by linking glycopeptide binding to cradle closure and catalysis, thereby expanding the host-glycan nutrient landscape accessible to infant-gut Bifidobacterium species.

title: Modeling the electricity system in integrated assessment models - a time-series clustering approach for diverse futures
abstract: The growing role of variable renewable electricity calls for high time resolution when modeling the electricity sector. However, this can be computationally too expensive for models that combine different sectors and run over long timeframes, such as Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs). The computational burden can be reduced by, e.g., timeslicing or time-series clustering. Clustering approaches have the benefit of maintaining chronology and thus enabling electricity storage modeling; however, which hourly-level features clustering should capture for the diverse long-term scenarios calculated with IAMs have remained unclear. This paper makes a two-fold contribution to address these challenges. First, we propose an hourly-resolution electricity sub-model that links to the annual level of a suitable IAM, and uses time-series clustering to reduce the hourly dimension to a small number of representative periods. Second, we propose a new clustering approach – the multi-scenario clustering – that functions robustly across a range of future scenarios that might be calculated with an IAM. In this approach, outputs from multiple model runs covering different future scenarios are used in clustering to define representative periods. Our results show that this approach produces a clustering that works for a wide range of future scenarios nearly as accurately as a-posteriori clustering tailored for each scenario individually. Therefore, the multi-scenario clustering approach provides a robust way to save on computational burden while offering a relatively good level of accuracy in comparison to using the full, multi-year, hourly time-horizon, which would be prohibitively costly to use in IAMs.

title: Differential methanogenic archaea-induced TLR8-dependent signaling engages gene classes regulated by NF-κB p65 and STAT1/2
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program but with distinct kinetics: M. stadtmanae triggered an earlier and stronger response, whereas M. smithii acted more gradually. Conserved early-upregulated genes separated into Class I genes, preferentially induced by M. stadtmanae, and Class II genes, similarly induced by both. M. stadtmanae showed greater early uptake, while responses to both archaea were broadly TLR8-dependent. ChIP-qPCR linked the stronger Class I gene activation induced by M. stadtmanae to greater NF-κB p65 binding at Class I promoters, whereas STAT1/2 binding at Class II promoters occurred with both stimuli. Dose-response analyses with archaeal RNA inputs supported distinct activation thresholds, with Class II genes at lower input and Class I genes requiring higher input. Together, these findings support an input-tuned TLR8-dependent mechanism shaping differential immune programs towards archaea.

title: UV Exposure and Durability of Emerging Photovoltaics: Quantifying and Reporting Outdoor UV Doses
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. Current accelerated UV tests, however, differ in spectral range and by orders of magnitude in intensity and dose. Their usual anchors, IEC 61215-2 preconditioning at 15 kW h m–2 and a fixed UV fraction of AM1.5G, do not represent long-term outdoor exposure. Here, we quantify annual outdoor UV doses (280–400 nm) across the contiguous United States from the National Solar Radiation Database for horizontal, fixed-tilt, and tracked mounting. Spectroradiometer measurements at two sites validate the model. Annual horizontal-plane doses span 72–133 kW h m–2, with a median of nearly 100 kW h m–2, so IEC 61215-2 preconditioning simulates only 1.4–2.5 months of outdoor exposure. Single-axis and dual-axis tracking typically add 10 and 18 kW h m–2, respectively. Finally, we propose reporting the source spectrum and expressing the test dose as a multiple of the annual outdoor dose for a stated location and mounting.

title: Diagnosis of Mechanisms of Kinetics in Lithium-Rich Manganese-Based Cathode Materials
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rate-determining step (RDS), which determines rate capability in lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials, remains unclear. In this work, we establish a quantitative diagnostic method for the RDS in LRMOs using in-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at different states of charge (SOC) and C-rates. From our results, the SOC determines the intrinsic bottleneck of the RDS, while the C-rate drives the transition from single-step to mixed control. Upon discharging to 4.4 V, the RDS is dominated by electron transfer at the interface accompanied by layered-to-spinel phase transition, whereas it is strongly influenced by solid-state diffusion in the bulk with depletion of Li vacancies arising from Jahn–Teller distortion when discharging to 3.0 V. Furthermore, Li+ diffusion, instead of charge transfer, plays a major part in the RDS of LRMOs when the C-rates are increased. These findings establish quantitative criteria for designing future cathode materials.

title: Culture-independent strain typing of Clostridioides difficile in fecal samples
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), the leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea, is a spore-forming obligate anaerobe that colonizes the intestinal tract and causes colitis in patients with compromised microbiome-mediated defenses. C. difficile is genomically diverse and is subtyped into ribotypes (RTs) and sequence types (STs) that vary in virulence and epidemic potential. Since secretion of the TcdB exotoxin is common to nearly all disease-associated C. difficile strains, PCR detection of TcdB has become a key clinical test used to diagnose C. difficile infection (CDI). This test and other available clinical laboratory tests, however, do not determine the prevalence of different C. difficile STs, making it impossible to identify transmission events or outbreaks in healthcare settings. Strain typing, because it requires technically demanding and time-consuming anaerobic fecal culturing of C. difficile, is not routinely performed, leaving healthcare epidemiologists unable to distinguish sporadic from epidemic occurrences of CDI. Herein, we optimized the established strain-level profiling tool, MetaPhlAn4 and StrainPhlAn, to distinguish C. difficile strains in the complex fecal microbiomes of hospitalized patients and demonstrate the utility of metagenomic short-read sequencing for culture-independent, rapid epidemiologic surveillance of CDI in healthcare environments.

title: PrinTE: a forward simulation framework for studying the role of transposable elements in genome expansion and contraction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Genome expansion and contraction are driven by transposable element activity, but the underlying dynamics remain enigmatic due to a lack of historical records tracing these changes. Here, we present PrinTE, a forward-time simulator of whole-genome sequences with customizable transposon dynamics for identifying the evolutionary parameters most consistent with an observed genome. Across simulations spanning four orders of magnitude, PrinTE recovers transposon insertion and deletion rates with less than 6% error. We demonstrate PrinTE on Arabidopsis and the fungal subdivision Pucciniomycotina, including myrtle rust (Austropuccinia psidii), which expanded its genome size to 1,018 Mb through transposon amplifications. Our simulations show that recombination-based removal of LTR retrotransposons alone cannot prevent genome obesity, and that preventing their invasion in the first place is more effective. We hypothesize that A. psidii might have experienced a prolonged expansion phase followed by a potent and ongoing period of contraction.

title: Grain boundary engineering using metallomesogen in formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide for stable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
abstract: Formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide perovskites show promise in terms of stability, yet their solar cell efficiency remains limited. Li et al. use a metallomesogen with mesophase to stabilize perovskite grain boundaries, improving both the efficiency and stability of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.

title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries are limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here the authors introduce a moderate-strain cyclic ether that redirects electrolyte decomposition to form a thin, robust interphase, thereby minimizing sodium consumption and extending cycling stability.

title: Directing solvent reactivity
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.

title: Rbpj restrains regulatory T cell exhaustion in tumors
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Although regulatory T (Treg) cells are vital for immune homeostasis and prevention of autoimmunity, they also exert an essential role in promoting tumor development. The mechanisms explaining why Treg cells remain functional in the hostile tumor microenvironment, while their effector counterparts become exhausted, remain incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that Treg-cell-specific deletion of Rbpj, the master transcription factor regulating Notch signaling, reduces tumor burden in mice. This is associated with the induction of an exhausted phenotype characterized by marked PD-1 upregulation. PD-1 deletion in Rbpj-deficient Treg cells reverses their exhausted phenotype and restores their tumor-promoting function. Finally, pharmacological inhibition of Rbpj using a novel small molecule promotes Treg cell exhaustion and reduces tumor growth. Collectively, our findings indicate that Notch-Rbpj signaling may act as an immune checkpoint pathway that hinders Treg exhaustion in tumors.

title: HuBMAP Data Portal: a resource for multimodal spatial and single-cell data of healthy human tissues
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) Data Portal (https://portal.hubmapconsortium.org/) serves as a comprehensive repository for multimodal, multi-scale spatial and single-cell data from healthy human tissues. As of August 2026, the portal hosts 9,316 public datasets from 26 data types spanning 29 organ classes across 501 donors. Portal infrastructure and user interfaces support data search and discovery, visualization, and analysis directly in web browsers. These capabilities include metadata- and data-driven search, collaborative Workspaces with access to high-performance compute, and interactive Vitessce visualizations across non-spatial, 2D, and 3D spatial datasets. Data-type-specific uniform processing pipelines and rigorous quality control processes ensure comparability of results across laboratories, organs, and donors, while externally processed community-contributed datasets provide complementary perspectives. Here we describe portal functionality, infrastructure, and design, and highlight its role as a platform for large-scale spatial single-cell research across diverse data types, organs, and scales.

title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Using laser microdissection, tissue-resolved metatranscriptomics, gnotobiotic hosts, and stable isotope tracing, we reveal that symbiosis profoundly restructures microbial communities across the epidermis and gastrodermis, enriching for taxa and pathways that support nitrogen assimilation in photosynthetically active tissues. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

title: An NLR protein with two distinct LRR domains mediates resistance to wheat powdery mildew
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Powdery mildew is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Aegilops caudata, a wild relative of common wheat, is highly resistant to powdery mildew. However, the presence of chromosomal structural variations and the absence of a reference genome for Ae. caudata have significantly hindered the cloning and breeding application of resistance genes from this species. Here, we report the cloning of powdery mildew resistance gene Pm7C from Ae. caudata by integrating map-based cloning, collinearity and Pm7C-direct donor transcriptome analysis. Pm7C encodes a nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) protein containing two distinct LRR domains. The resistance function of Pm7C is validated by mutagenesis, gene silencing and transgenic assay. The coiled coil (CC) domain of Pm7C induces cell death and self-associates. Additionally, we develop a set of Pm7C introgression lines and a Pm7C-specific diagnostic molecular marker. Cloning of Pm7C will shed light on NLR protein-mediated disease resistance and accelerate its deployment in wheat breeding.

title: Potassium-ion batteries for stationary energy storage solutions
abstract: Potassium-ion batteries are a potentially sustainable and cost-competitive technology for large-scale stationary energy storage.

title: Polymorph-tuned photoinduced red luminescence and room-temperature phosphorescence in macrocyclic molecular crystals
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the increasing demand, fabricating organic functional molecular crystals with highly tunable photoluminescent properties in the same system remains a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that photoinduced red emission and room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) can be effectively regulated via crystal-polymorph modulation in a macrocyclic diphenylamine[3]arene (DPA[3]) compound. During crystal growth, kinetic control directs DPA[3] molecules to adopt distinct stacking motifs, resulting in two polymorphs (Type A and Type B) with divergent luminescent properties. Type A crystals exhibit photoinduced red emission extending to 630 nm, while Type B crystals show long-lived green RTP (lifetime >450 ms) after ultraviolet light excitation. Notably, thermal treatment of Type A crystals induces a partial polymorphic evolution toward the Type B crystals. Experimental and calculation analyses reveal that paired DPA[3] molecules in Type A form a columnar packing motif, which may facilitate photoinduced electron transfer to generate charge transfer intermediates for red luminescence. In contrast, Type B crystals feature a more distorted herringbone stacking motif with a tighter molecular stacking structure, enabling stabilizing triplet excitons that support efficient RTP. Our findings present an effective strategy for achieving single-component materials with multiple luminescent functionalities by regulating the aggregate state.

title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Efficient construction of the trans-decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis.
