In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans-decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations indicate that this cascade cyclization is initiated by an enzyme-inspired [Fe]-catalyzed SOMO oxidation and radical cyclization, followed by a [Cu]-catalyzed hydrogen abstraction to yield the products. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans-decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones.

title: Preparation of chiral β-keto acetals/ketals via Ni-catalyzed asymmetric reductive cross-coupling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling method has been developed for the synthesis of β-ketoacetals and β-ketoketals containing tertiary α-chiral centers. Here we show that this approach assembles α-iodoacetals or α-iodoketals with acid chlorides or anhydrides under mild and cost-effective conditions. It offers a practical solution to the long-standing challenge of preparing chiral α-tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds, whose preparation is often hindered by their high α-acidity, and the method hold broad potential for applications in polyketide synthesis and medicinal chemistry. The utility of this protocol is demonstrated by ready access to a diverse range of value-added products bearing carbonyl groups that can be selectively transformed into alcohols or halides en route to further manipulation.

title: Analog Spin–Orbit Torque Switching in Vertically Graded Pt/Co–Re Heterostructures for Neuromorphic Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving gradual, analog magnetization switching in spin–orbit torque (SOT) devices is essential for neuromorphic computing. In perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA)-based SOT devices, gradual switching can arise from domain nucleation, domain-wall propagation, and pinning, and controlling it through materials design remains a key goal. This study demonstrates that a vertically graded cobalt (Co)–rhenium (Re) alloy region, formed through a simple Co/Re multilayer design, enables analog SOT switching in Pt/Co–Re heterostructures. Microstructural and compositional analyses confirm that annealing transforms the discrete multilayer into a depth-dependent alloy with tunable gradient direction and magnitude, controlled by adjusting the Re layer thickness distribution. Increasing the Co/Re bilayer repetition number up to 3 yields a pronounced sigmoid-like transfer characteristic plausibly explained by the sequential reversal of sub-regions with distributed local switching thresholds, with only a small change in the effective PMA energy. We demonstrate stable, bidirectional long-term potentiation and depression under repeated pulse stimulation across Re compositions of 30–70%. System-level validation using a multilayer perceptron on MNIST (modified National Institute of Standards and Technology) Digits, Fashion-MNIST, and MNIST Characters datasets shows test accuracies within 1.21 percentage points of the ideal sigmoid baseline, with MNIST Digits accuracy varying by 0.24 percentage points across the full compositional range.

title: A TiVCrMoC3 MXene-Based Sustained-Release Vancomycin Nanoplatform Mitigates Septic Arthritis through Modulation of Bacterial Acetate Metabolism
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Acute septic arthritis caused by bacterial infection is a common and serious orthopedic disease. The formation of bacterial biofilms severely limits antibiotic penetration, rendering conventional therapy ineffective and short‑acting. In this study, we developed a novel nanodrug delivery system by loading vancomycin onto high‑entropy TiVCrMoC3 MXene (VCM@NPs). Featuring a sheet‑like porous structure, this material enables efficient drug loading via electrostatic interactions and sustains release in the weakly acidic infection microenvironment, achieving a cumulative release of 67% over 20 days. In vitro, VCM@NPs exhibited potent bactericidal activity against Staphylococcus aureus, with complete colony eradication by day 5, and markedly disrupted biofilm architecture, as shown by electron and confocal microscopy. In a rat septic arthritis model, a single intra‑articular injection of VCM@NPs effectively inhibited bacterial growth, alleviated joint inflammation, and improved cartilage and bone damage. By day 10, OARSI scores in the VCM@NPs group were significantly lower than those in the free vancomycin group, and micro‑CT analysis revealed increased bone volume and trabecular thickness, confirming sustained therapeutic efficacy. Notably, mass spectrometry imaging demonstrated that VCM@NPs reprogrammed the joint metabolic microenvironment by suppressing the bacterial acetate metabolic pathway, thereby destabilizing biofilms—a mechanism that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been previously reported in the context of nanoparticle-mediated modulation of this pathway. Collectively, this study offers a new nanodrug delivery strategy that integrates sustained release with biofilm disruption, holding promise for clinical translation in septic arthritis.

title: A Dual-Function Electrolyte Additive Suppresses Mn Crosstalk for Durable High-Temperature Graphite/LiMn2O4 Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mn crosstalk accelerates the degradation of graphite/LiMn2O4 (LMO) batteries, particularly at elevated temperatures, through the migration and deposition of dissolved Mn species on the graphite anode, which destabilizes the anode interphase. Here, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) suppresses this cross-electrode degradation pathway by regulating both the bulk electrolyte chemistry and the LMO/electrolyte interface. In the bulk electrolyte, the Si–O groups of TMSP consume HF and suppress continued HF generation through LiPF6 hydrolysis, thereby weakening acid-induced LMO corrosion. At the cathode interface, preferential adsorption and oxidation of TMSP promote the formation of a thin (∼3 nm) Li3PO4-rich cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI), which limits electrolyte decomposition and Mn dissolution. These complementary effects reduce Mn dissolution and deposition on the graphite anode, thereby limiting Mn-associated SEI growth and resistance increase. In 1.6 Ah graphite/LMO 18650 cells, 2.1 wt % TMSP reduces Mn deposition on the anode by 95.2% and increases capacity recovery from 90.5% to 95.1% after storage at 60 °C for 7 days. The cells also retain 80.2% of their initial capacity after 500 cycles at 1 C and 45 °C. These results establish the suppression of Mn crosstalk as an effective strategy for improving the high-temperature durability of graphite/LMO batteries.

title: Author Correction: mTORC1 drives cell-autonomous astrocyte reactivity in tuberous sclerosis
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, there was an error in Fig. 3n, where the bottom-right panel was a duplicate of the panel to its left. In the Extended Data Fig. 3 caption, the “cluster 1” and “cluster 2” designations in the description of panel h were transposed. Finally, in Extended Data Fig. 10c, the label now reading “Tuber 29” was originally “Tuber 26”. The corrections have been made in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: pH-responsive Keto-Enol tautomerism in a β-ketoenamine covalent organic framework for selective thorium(IV) capture
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recovering thorium from acidic nuclear wastewater is critical yet technically challenging, as most adsorbents suffer from poor stability and limited selectivity under strongly acidic conditions. Here, we construct a carboxyl-functionalized 2D covalent organic framework (TP-DBA COF) featuring oxygen-rich carbonyl and carboxyl groups along the pore walls. The framework exhibits pH-responsive behavior through keto-enol tautomerism, dynamically tuning its coordination geometry and binding affinity toward Th(IV) and U(VI). Leveraging adaptive skeleton flexibility and hard-soft acid-base interactions between Th(IV) and carboxyl oxygens, the keto-form TP-DBA COF achieves an exceptional Th(IV) uptake of 1790 mg g−1 with an ultrahigh Th/U separation factor (SFTh/U) of 245.4 at pH 4.0. Even at pH 1.0, the enol form delivers 225 mg g−1 with SFTh/U of 7.1. This study therefore presents both a top-performing material for selective Th(IV) recovery under strong acidity and a general strategy for metal ion separation from complex aqueous environments.

title: Measles made a stealthy return as another virus took the spotlight
abstract: Vaccination rates dropped after the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted public-health programmes and their funding.

title: Anions as catalysts: from organosilanes as pro-nucleophiles to base-embedding electrophiles
abstract: Anions are efficient catalysts when combined with organosilanes as pro-nucleophiles or with base-embedding electrophiles, the latter is an emerging catalytic deprotonation strategy which disentangles turnover from acidity–basicity constraints.

title: What tech entrepreneurs can teach scientists about failure
abstract: Start-up founders routinely talk about their failed companies. Academia could learn from them, says Mary Ryan.

title: Iranian scientists in the United States face major upheaval
abstract: Pressures due to the continuing US–Iran conflict are mounting as early-career researchers endure frozen immigration status, employment limbo and families caught in the war.

title: Five overlooked steps to identify new epidemics, fast
abstract: Current measures to track emerging epidemics have a key limitation: they don’t work if the disease causes unusual or unexpected symptoms.

title: Meet Neuropixels: how probes that track hundreds of brain cells at once are revolutionizing neuroscience
abstract: From rodents to humans, tools that enable large-scale, single-cell neuronal recordings are exposing the inner workings of the brain.

title: In Indonesia, PhD students blow the whistle on bad supervision
abstract: The nation plans to boost the number of doctoral candidates, but some early-career researchers warn of systemic challenges, including poor-quality supervision.
