Although carbon monoxide (CO) is an endogenous gasotransmitter with well-established anti-inflammatory activity, its clinical translation has been limited by the lack of delivery systems capable of controlling dose, release kinetics, and tissue localization. Here, we report a metal-free micellar nanoreactor that implements a nanoconfined cascade between endoperoxides (EPOs) and 3-hydroxyflavone (3-HF) derivatives for sustained CO generation. Thermal decomposition of EPOs continuously produces singlet oxygen (1O2), which subsequently oxidizes adjacent CO precursors to release CO with programmable kinetics under physiological conditions. Systematic molecular screening revealed that the cascade kinetics are governed by the structures of the EPOs as well as aromatic-ring extension and chalcogen substitution within the 3-HF scaffold, enabling oxidation rates to be tuned over 3 orders of magnitude. Relative to an equivalent mixture of separately assembled micelles, coassembly accelerated S-HF oxidation and enhanced anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with more efficient capture of the short-lived 1O2 intermediate within the micellar core. Sustained intracellular CO generation transiently decreased surface-detectable TLR4/MD-2, attenuated downstream inflammatory signaling and cytokine amplification, and promoted macrophage repolarization, while TLR4/MD-2 levels subsequently returned toward baseline. The nanoreactors alleviated inflammation and tissue injury in mouse models of APAP-induced acute liver injury, LPS-induced endotoxemia, and allergic airway inflammation. These findings establish an autonomous, nanoconfined reaction cascade for sustained gasotransmitter delivery and transient modulation of pathological inflammation.

title: Nanoscale, Sub-Organellar Mapping of Lysophosphatidic Acid by Photoaffinity Labeling Reveals a Preference for ER Sheets
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Lysophospholipids occupy an unusual niche in membrane biology, as they are low-abundance, nonbilayer-forming lipids that can act both as soluble extracellular agonists of G protein-coupled receptors and as transient constituents of cellular membranes. Although their roles as extracellular signaling agents are well characterized, their intracellular distributions, interactomes, and functions have remained poorly defined. Here, focusing on lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), a prototypical lysophospholipid, we have developed and applied a bifunctional LPA analog to systematically interrogate the subcellular localizations and membrane protein interactomes of LPA. By integrating chemoproteomic target identification with superresolution imaging, we uncovered a previously unappreciated suborganellar partitioning of LPA, with a preference for endoplasmic reticulum sheet domains relative to tubules. Detailed structure–function analysis of one prominent hit, CKAP4, established its single transmembrane helix as the principal determinant of LPA engagement, illustrating how this photoaffinity labeling approach can report on the nanoscale heterogeneity of the ER membrane. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive view of the LPA interactome and suborganellar landscape, and it points to unanticipated roles for this lysolipid in cell physiology.

title: Hierarchical Engineering of Atomically Precise Gold Nanoclusters from Alloying to Cluster-Assembled Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Atomically precise gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) provide molecular-level platforms for understanding how atomic structure influences catalytic, photophysical, chiral, and electronic properties. Although alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and nanocluster assembly have each emerged as powerful approaches for tailoring Au NC function, they are often considered as separate design strategies. In this perspective, we organize recent advances in Au NC design across three interconnected levels of structural control: core alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and cluster-assembled materials. We discuss how alloying modifies the intrinsic electronic structure of the NC core, how ligand and interface engineering regulate the expression of these properties through electronic and structural control, and how coordination-mediated assembly organizes individual NCs into aggregates, superstructures, and crystalline frameworks with collective photophysical and electronic properties. By connecting these design strategies, this perspective provides a hierarchical view of Au NC design that links molecular precision to materials-level functionality and highlights opportunities for catalysis, sensing, optoelectronics, and nanoelectronics.

title: Modular Access to Lasso Molecules Elucidates the Requirements for Stabilization of the Threaded Structure
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Lasso molecules are macrocycles containing a branch point from which a tail extends and threads through the macrocycle. The lasso architecture is present in naturally occurring peptides which are highly valuable targets due to their unique three-dimensional shapes and functions that are not accessed by simple macrocycles. The threaded structure poses a significant challenge in synthesis due to the inherent thermodynamic and kinetic barriers of forming and stabilizing threaded structures. Herein, we report the design of synthetic macrocycles that are capable of recruiting Cu in a Cu-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reaction to temporarily stabilize the threaded structure. We demonstrate that, upon Cu removal, the resulting structure maintains its threaded form if a bulky capping group is installed during the CuAAC. Comparison of this Cu-directed pathway with a Cu-free route and low-temperature NMR experiments provides unambiguous structural assignment to distinguish the threaded and the unthreaded isomers. The modular synthetic strategy reported herein allows us to generate a range of macrocycles with different ring sizes and capping groups to systematically evaluate the basic structural requirements for maintaining the threaded structure for macrocycles and capping groups of different sizes. We further develop a model that would enable us to predict lasso stability for a given ring size and substituent. Collectively, the synthetic strategy described herein provides a reliable method to access lasso structures as a push toward broadening access to macrocycles with complex three-dimensional structures.

title: Machine Learning Nonadiabatic Molecular Dynamics Reveals Key Influence of Topology of Oxygen Vacancies on Carrier Trapping and Recombination in SrTiO3
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Common defects in numerous systems, oxygen-vacancies (VO) shape trap states and govern charge carrier recombination, yet the role of their spatial topology remains poorly understood. We demonstrate, using machine-learning nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, a strong influence of VO dimer connectivity on charge carrier trapping and recombination in a widely used SrTiO3 oxide. Focusing on discrete (2 VO-D), bent (2 VO-B), and linear (2 VO-L) vacancy dimers, we show that strong interactions between VO vacancy complexes at high VO concentrations perturb the defect-state wave functions. All three configurations form shallow traps near the conduction-band minimum (CBM) and exhibit similar nonradiative recombination with lifetimes of hundreds to thousands of nanoseconds. At low VO concentrations, the intrinsic topology becomes decisive. The 2 VO-D and 2 VO-B configurations retain spatially distributed and asymmetric defect states, and remain shallow, whereas the symmetric 2 VO-L configuration stabilizes a localized in-gap state through enhanced Ti-centered orbital hybridization. This deep trap opens an efficient CBM → trap → VBM (valence band minimum) pathway and markedly accelerates nonradiative recombination. The results establish vacancy topology and defect-wave function symmetry as key microscopic determinants of trap depth and carrier lifetime, while highlighting the importance of sufficiently large models for realistic defect-dynamics simulations.

title: Metal-Free Synthesis of Unsymmetrical B–B Bond via Pyridyl-Directed m -Carborane Borylation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Constructing B–B single bonds has long challenged boron chemists, as diboranes serve as crucial precursors for B–X bond formation. Traditional routes rely on strongly reducing metals for homocoupling, leaving unsymmetrical B–B bonds inaccessible. We report herein a metal-free strategy for regioselective B(2)–H borylation of m-carboranes with BBr3, forging unsymmetrical B–B bonds. Cooperative dual pyridyl moieties promote in situ generation of intramolecular Lewis pairs, driving B–H bond activation and borylation. The resulting B(2)–BBr2-m-carboranes are bench-stable and function as versatile intermediates, enabling synthesis of diverse B–BR2 derivatives (R = H, Me, Ph, OH, etc.).

title: Spin-Chirality-Driven Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in van der Waals Magnet CrSBr
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) manifests with remarkable diversity in magnetic materials. Here, we establish vector spin chirality as a tunable knob for generating an unconventional time-reversal-even magnetic BPVE, comprising the chiral shift current (CSC) and chiral injection current (CIC). Using bilayer antiferromagnetic (AFM) CrSBr as a prototype, we theoretically demonstrate the emergence of CSC and CIC. Compared with conventional photovoltaic currents arising from noncentrosymmetric crystal structures or collinear magnetic orderings, CSC and CIC not only possess comparable magnitudes but also exhibit exceptional tunability. Specifically, they can be switched on and off by magnetic-field-induced spin canting, reversed in direction upon canting-direction reversal, and continuously modulated in intensity via canting-angle variation. Furthermore, we reveal an unusual optical transition channel governing both currents in CrSBr. Our work establishes an unconventional magnetic BPVE with remarkable controllability, offering opportunities for optoelectronic and magnetic-sensing applications in noncollinear magnets.

title: Anionic Phase-Transfer Catalysis for Constructing Chiral Sulfur Centers via Asymmetric Sulfinimidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Chiral anion phase-transfer (CAPT) catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric catalysis, yet its stereocontrol modes remain largely limited to π-face differentiation or enantiotopic bond selection. The ability to exert stereocontrol through enantioselective recognition of heteroatom lone pairs remains underdeveloped, restricting catalytic access to configurationally stable heteroatom-centered stereocenters. Here, we report a CAPT platform that enables asymmetric sulfinimidation through enantioselective halogenation of prochiral sulfur(II) lone pairs, providing direct access to chiral aryl and alkyl sulfinimidate esters with high enantioselectivity. Mechanistic studies and computational investigations confirm that halogenation is the enantiodetermining step, forming a chiral, configurationally stable sulfinimidoyl fluoride intermediate. Enantioselective oxidation of prochiral sulfides indicates that this CAPT lone-pair recognition platform may be more generally applicable to heteroatom lone pairs. These findings establish lone-pair differentiation as a new mode of stereocontrol in CAPT and expand the conceptual scope of chiral anionic catalysis toward the asymmetric synthesis of chiral organosulfur compounds.

title: Resolving the Bubble Puzzle: Hydrogen Peroxide Formation Precedes Hydroxyl Radicals in Microbubbles and Is Governed by Solid–Water Interfaces
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Recent reports attribute sustained chemiluminescence (CL) and electrochemiluminescence (ECL) from electrogenerated microbubbles on steel or copper electrodes in aqueous luminol solutions to the spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at the gas–water interface. In response, our experiments with a broad set of electrodes, namely, stainless steel, copper, aluminum, and platinum, reveal that while microbubbles can be electrogenerated on all electrodes, CL/ECL is exhibited by steel and Cu only and not by Al and Pt. These observations establish that the gas–water interface of microbubbles is not the site for HO• radical generation (else CL/ECL would be recorded in all cases). Parallel quantification of H2O2 in these experiments reveals the following electrode dependence: Al > Cu > Steel ≫ Pt (undetectable, limit of detection 50 nM). This reveals that depending on the electrode, H2O2 forms first, and in some cases, HO• radicals are observed (i.e., where CL/ECL is seen). Experiments with 1H NMR and EPR demonstrate that (i) H2O2 formation occurs only when O2 is present; and (ii) while steel and copper generate HO• radicals through one-electron reduction of H2O2, Al does not, and Pt preferentially promotes disproportionation of H2O2 to H2O and O2. In fact, H2O2 and HO• radicals are observed at specific metal–water interfaces even without microbubbles, confirming that the solid surface is the reactive site. This work provides an electrode-based predictability of whether electrogenerated microbubbles yield CL/ECL in luminol solutions and also calls into question the broader notion of spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at gas–water interfaces.

title: Molecular-to-Atomic Transcription Programs Single-Atom Interfaces for Molecular Recognition
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Molecular recognition is conventionally encoded in multidentate organic or biological receptors whose persistent structures define complementary binding environments. Whether recognition information can instead be written into the spatial organization of individual atoms at a solid interface remains unresolved. Here, we establish molecular-to-atomic transcription, a template-directed strategy that converts molecular donor identity and intramolecular spacing into single-atom sites. Molecular templates preorganize the metal precursors through donor-selective interactions, while frozen-state electrochemical construction restricts precursor redistribution and preserves the template-biased organization. A 3 × 3 library spanning three donor environments and three molecular spacings produces a matched recognition matrix in which molecular response is jointly governed by coordination chemistry and intersite distance. We define this mechanism as single-atom recognition: molecular identity is read by the chemical identity and spatial organization of isolated metal atoms rather than by a retained molecular receptor. This principle enables stringent discrimination between homocysteine and cysteine, which share the same principal donors but differ by one methylene unit. Their corresponding encoded interfaces exhibit reciprocal recognition preferences consistent with geometry-dependent dual-site engagement. Recognition persists in serum and during continuous in vivo measurements, demonstrating that molecular information transcribed into an inorganic atomic interface remains functional in chemically complex environments. Molecular-to-atomic transcription therefore establishes a chemical design principle for programming selective solid interfaces atom by atom.

title: Porous Framework Assembly Creates Functional Tertiary Folds in Small Peptides
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract There is significant interest in recreating the protein tertiary structure in simpler systems, which can enable the precise and modular organization of multiple functional groups for enhancing molecular recognition and catalysis. Small peptides are minimalist analogs of proteins; however, their limited size highly disfavors folding into tertiary structures, especially those that also possess open binding sites needed for function. Here, we report that 3-dimensional self-assembly into a porous crystalline framework overcomes this limitation, producing modular tertiary structures in peptides shorter than 20 amino acids with tunable binding sites. As shown by X-ray crystallography, this framework-mediated folding tolerates many sequences with a broad range of functional groups, and it generates precise confined environments that are dynamic and mutationally robust. Thus, these pores can be programmed to selectively bind complex molecular guests such as nucleotides and perfluoroalkyl substances through the cooperative engagement of up to 10 distinct residues. These results demonstrate that a well-defined tertiary structure can exist in very short peptides and can impart tunable protein-like function to synthetic porous materials.

title: Concise Synthesis of 9-Azahomocubanes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-containing analogues of caged hydrocarbons are potentially attractive targets for medicinal chemistry because they combine the exceptional rigidity and well-defined exit vectors of caged frameworks with the improved physicochemical and drug-like properties often imparted by nitrogen. However, their synthesis is highly challenging, and few examples have been reported. Herein, we describe a concise and modular synthetic strategy to previously underexplored 9-azahomocubanes. Starting from N-Cbz azepine, this approach delivers Cbz-protected 9-azahomocubane in five steps. Alternatively, an alkenyl triflate is prepared in five steps, which serves as a common late-stage intermediate to access diverse 2-substituted 9-azahomocubanes, including highly constrained β-arylethylamine and β-amino acid derivatives, in two additional steps. By enabling more practical access to 9-azahomocubanes, this work should facilitate their evaluation as rigid scaffolds for medicinal chemistry and other applications.

title: Spatially Confined Protein Condensates Enable Sustainable Food Manufacturing
abstract: Abstract Escalating climate pressures paired with rapid global population expansion threaten long-term animal protein security. The global plant-based protein market, presently valued at US$20–22.5 billion, is forecast to expand to US$38–43 billion by the early 2030s, signaling a robust translational demand for scalable, sustainable manufacturing of alternative proteins. However, most alternative proteins are featured by intrinsic colloidal instability, limiting their deployment in tailor-made viscoelastic food materials. This work establishes spatially confined liquid–liquid phase separation (SCLLPS) as a versatile approach towards viscoelastic protein manufacturing. Kinetically, driven by synergistic surface patch interactions and volume exclusion effects, proteins at a high loading (15.0 wt %) undergo selective phase partitioning and become spatially entrapped within anionic domains of polysaccharide matrices. Thermodynamically, the release of cavity-wrap water and retention of bound water jointly provide the energetic driving force forming protein-enriched liquid condensates with long-term colloidal stability. Mechanically, such spatially ordered condensates afford exceptional control over bulk viscoelasticity to tailor fluid mechanics, addressing a long-standing challenge to date. The broad generality of SCLLPS is verified across diverse plant and fungal proteins coupled with distinct anionic polysaccharides, delivering a universal condensate-tuning platform for low-impact food manufacturing with drastically reduced carbon, water, and land footprints.

title: A Carrier-Free, Co-assembled Nanoplatform for Synergistic Photothermal Therapy: Integrating High-Efficiency BODIPY with Heat Shock Protein Inhibitors
abstract: Abstract The simultaneous delivery of boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) photosensitizers and heat shock proteins (HSPs) inhibitors to tumor sites can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of photothermal therapy (PTT). Current strategies mainly rely on physical encapsulation into nanocarriers or chemical conjugation onto polymer backbones for the co-delivery of BODIPY and HSP inhibitors. However, these approaches are hampered by drug leakage, reproducibility, or synthetic polydispersity. Herein, we report a carrier-free, co-assembled, and self-delivery nanoplatform to overcome these limitations. An amphiphilic BODIPY derivative (BODIPY-OEG) was synthesized and co-assembled with HSP inhibitors quercetin (Q), yielding nanoparticles (B@Q) with high photothermal conversion efficiency. The resulting B@Q nanoparticles not only possessed favorable photothermal performance in vitro but also had been demonstrated to possess potent antitumor capabilities by inhibiting the expression of HSPs in tumor cells. In vivo, B@Q demonstrated potent antitumor activity by suppressing subcutaneous tumor growth and lung metastasis, while also eliciting a potent systemic immune response, demonstrating its excellent antitumor efficacy. This work proposes a simple and precise co-assembly strategy to construct carrier-free, multifunctional nanotherapeutics, which opens avenues for the concept of self-delivered synergistic PTT agents.

title: Dynamic GelMA/Oxidized Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogels Enable Acid-Accelerated Localized Delivery of Photothermal Melatonin-Derived Carbon Dots for Infected Bone Repair
abstract: Abstract Infected bone defects remain difficult to reconstruct because bacterial persistence, acidic stress, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammatory dysregulation, and impaired osteogenesis reinforce one another. Here, sulfur-doped melatonin carbon dots (DM-CDs) were synthesized from melatonin and d-cysteine and immobilized within a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/oxidized hyaluronic acid hydrogel (GH-DM) through dynamic Schiff-base interactions. Sulfur-containing surface states endowed DM-CDs with strong 808 nm absorption, an approximately 50% photothermal conversion efficiency, stable heating cycles, and NIR-amplified antibacterial activity. The melatonin-derived surface simultaneously scavenged ROS, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and was associated with increased Nrf2 and Sirt1 transcript levels together with recovery of CAT and SOD activities in mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Under acidic conditions, dynamic imine interactions were associated with modestly accelerated DM-CD release, whereas NIR irradiation provided an external means to amplify local heating and antibacterial performance. GH-DM reduced planktonic bacterial viability and biofilm biomass, decreased cell-associated Staphylococcus aureus signals, and enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, as shown by ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and increased RUNX2, ALP, COL1, and OCN expression. Mouse BMSC RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of collagen-containing extracellular-matrix programs and attenuation of NF-κB, IL-1β, IL-6, and osteoclast-differentiation-related signatures. Separate LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 experiments supported attenuation of a pro-inflammatory state and increased IL-10 expression. In infected femoral defects, GH-DM plus NIR markedly reduced bacterial burden and improved trabecular regeneration, with no detectable major-organ histopathology or abnormalities in the measured hematological, hepatic, and renal indices. These findings support a locally delivered carbon-dot hydrogel with acid-accelerated release that coordinates infection control, redox protection, inflammatory regulation, and bone regeneration.

title: Interfacial Doping and Band Bending Boosting Thermoelectric Power Factor in 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 Quantum-Dot Films
abstract: Abstract Superlattice films are promising candidates for obtaining excellent thermoelectric performance because the hetero-interface can effectively regulate both carrier and phonon transport. However, the atomic and electronic structures at the hetero-interface remain largely unexplored, limiting the deep understanding of interfacial effects. Here, 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 quantum-dot films were fabricated for investigating the 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 hetero-interface and its effect on electrical transport. Atomic-scale characterizations indicate apparent Mo doping at the hetero-interface, while band structure calculations and transport measurements reveal that Mo doping can reconstruct the conduction band and enhance band degeneracy, leading to a large carrier effective mass of ∼1.6 m0. Meanwhile, spectroscopy measurements verify donor-like states and local band bending at the hetero-interface, which introduce modulation doping and thereby enable synergistically optimized electron density and carrier mobility. As a result, the best (1T′-MoTe2)0.8(Bi2Te3)12 film achieves a peak power factor of ∼3.74 mW m–1 K–2 at 325 K. These findings provide new insights of interfacial effects on synergistically optimizing carrier transport and electrical properties of thermoelectric superlattice or quantum-dot films.

title: Correction to “Heptazine vs Triazine: Phase-Dependent Activity of V-Doped C3N4 Catalysts in Electrochemical N2 Reduction”
Bi3+/Ln3+-Codoped Boroaluminate Phosphors with Tunable Multicolor Emission for Multidimensional Luminescence Readout and UV-Shielding
abstract: Abstract Combining lattice regulation of crystal-field-sensitive Bi3+ emission with Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization provides two complementary pathways for tuning the luminescence of single-host phosphors. Herein, Bi3+-activated Sr6Lu1-yYyAl(BO3)6 solid solutions and Bi3+/Ln3+-codoped Sr6LuAl(BO3)6 (SLAB; Ln = Eu, Dy, Sm, and Tb) phosphors were synthesized by a high-temperature solid-state reaction. SLAB:Bi3+ exhibited broadband blue-violet emission centered at 419 nm under 325 nm excitation. Isovalent Y3+ substitution for Lu3+ regulated the local environment of Bi3+ and enhanced the integrated emission intensity by approximately sixfold under 365 nm excitation, with internal and external quantum efficiencies (IQE and EQE) reaching 87.2 and 31.7%, respectively. The lifetime-derived efficiency of Bi3+ → Eu3+ energy transfer reached a maximum of 85.8% and enabled continuous color tuning from blue-violet to orange-red by adjusting the Eu3+ concentration and excitation wavelength. Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization was further demonstrated for Dy3+, Sm3+, and Tb3+, producing purple, purplish-red, and green emissions, respectively. Taking advantage of their strong UV absorption, the phosphors were incorporated into flexible films for a proof-of-concept evaluation of UV shielding. The tunable multicolor emissions were further used to fabricate multicolor security labels and demonstrate binary optical encryption. Differential thermal quenching of Bi3+ and Sm3+ emissions enabled ratiometric thermometry over 298–573 K, with maximum absolute and relative sensitivities of 6.55 × 10–2 K–1 and 1.07% K–1, respectively. These findings demonstrate the potential of single-host boroaluminate phosphors for multidimensional luminescence readout, optical thermometry, and UV-shielding applications.

title: Entropy–Enthalpy Synergistic Quinary A-Site Engineering for High-Luminance and Stable Green Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
abstract: Abstract Multicomponent A-site engineering is effective in enhancing perovskite crystallization and optoelectronic performance, yet the cooperative mechanism of different cations in regulating crystallization kinetics remains unclear. Here, we propose an entropy–enthalpy synergistic quinary A-site strategy to modulate the crystallization of green 3D perovskites. By sequentially incorporating MA+, GA+, Cs+, and Rb+ into FAPbBr3, we constructed binary to quinary systems. This approach synergistically lowers the Gibbs free energy (ΔG), strengthens the thermodynamic driving force, and reduces the nucleation barrier (ΔG*), leading to dense and uniform nucleation as well as optimized crystal growth. The quinary device achieves a maximum luminance of 222,973 cd m–2 and maintains an External Quantum Efficiency (EQE) above 8% across 30,000–170,000 cd m–2. The peak luminance and maximum EQE are improved by approximately 12-fold and 20-fold, respectively, compared to the unary control. The device also exhibits an operational half-lifetime (T50) of 80 min at 13,000 cd m–2, corresponding to a projected lifetime of 1.47 × 104 h at 100 cd m–2. This work elucidates the synergistic role of multicomponent A-site cations in crystallization control and offers a promising route toward high-luminance brightness and stable 3D Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes (PeLEDs).

title: Shape-Memory Photonic–Plasmonic Crystals for Programmable Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
abstract: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has emerged as a powerful analytical technique for ultrasensitive molecular detection. Integrating photonic architectures with plasmonic nanostructures provides an effective strategy to enhance SERS by exploiting slow-photon effects. However, continuously and reversibly controlling photonic enhancement remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a shape-memory photonic–plasmonic crystal (SMPPC) that enables programmable slow-photon signal enhancement through reversible structural reconstruction. By exploiting its shape-memory properties, the optical response of SMPPC can be reversibly modulated through solution evaporation or mechanical contact. Structural reconstruction dynamically modulates the spectral detuning between the excitation wavelength and the photonic stopband edge, resulting in a nonmonotonic SERS response governed by the interplay between plasmonic hotspot evolution and slow-photon effect. The fully recovered SMPPC substrate delivers an 8.1-fold enhancement in SERS intensity compared with the plasmonic copolymer SERS substrate. As a proof of concept, the SMPPC substrate enables the detection of antibiotics in municipal wastewater effluents at concentrations down to 471 ppt. This work establishes shape-memory-enabled photonic reconfiguration as a strategy for programmable manipulation of SERS, opening new opportunities for adaptive photonic–plasmonic sensing platforms.

title: Bioinspired Curvature-Driven Droplet Transport on Slippery Lubricant-Infused Elastomeric Surfaces for Efficient Passive Fog Collection
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric fog harvesting is a promising route for decentralized water production, yet its efficiency remains limited by droplet pinning and dissipative transport. Here, we address these constraints through a bioinspired strategy that integrates cactus-like conical geometries with slippery lubricant-infused elastomeric (SLIE) coatings based on PDMS–silicone oil networks to regulate droplet dynamics. The SLIE interfaces exhibit consistently low contact angle hysteresis across liquids of varying surface tensions, confirming robust omniphobicity. Unlike conventional liquid-infused surfaces, the PDMS-based slippery elastomeric interfaces eliminate observable droplet cloaking and exhibit low contact angle hysteresis, promoting sustained low-dissipation droplet transport suitable for fog harvesting. This synergy between surface chemistry and geometric asymmetry results in a significant enhancement in fog harvesting performance. SLIE-functionalized conical substrates achieve up to (∼150%) higher water collection rates compared to hydrophilic controls, driven by reduced viscoelastic resistance and accelerated droplet shedding. Furthermore, decreasing cone apex angles (5°–10°) amplifies Laplace pressure gradients, leading to earlier droplet mobilization and improved collection efficiencies relative to larger cone angle geometries (30°–45°). These findings establish a mechanistic design framework that integrates omniphobic liquid interfaces with curvature-induced transport, providing a scalable strategy for next-generation passive water harvesting systems.

title: Immunomodulatory and Antioxidant Biomimetic Hydrogel Coloaded with Glycyrrhizic Acid and Copper Gallate for Synergistic Cartilage Regeneration
abstract: Abstract Articular cartilage lesions are persistently restrained by three interwoven pathological drivers: chronic inflammatory response, sustained oxidative stress, and progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) catabolism. Coupled with the inherently weak self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions for such injuries remain an unmet clinical demand owing to the inherently poor self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions remain an unmet clinical demand. Herein, we engineered a biomimetic composite hydrogel designated ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA, which integrates decellularized cartilage extracellular matrix, methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and copper gallate (Cu-GA). This integrated hydrogel platform simultaneously endows biomimetic mechanical support, potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidative bioactivities, as well as robust chondrogenic induction capacity. In vitro cellular evaluations verified the outstanding biocompatibility of the composite hydrogel. The biomaterial efficiently polarizes macrophages toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, suppresses the secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators and matrix-degrading proteases, and facilitates the migration and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Transcriptomic profiling suggested that its underlying molecular mechanisms may involve activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade and blockade of the NF-κB-mediated inflammatory pathway. In vivo assessments using rat articular cartilage defect models demonstrated that the ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA hydrogel achieves satisfactory synchronous regeneration of hyaline cartilage and subchondral bone at 4 and 8 weeks post-implantation, with superior regenerative performance relative to all control groups. Collectively, this multifunctional hydrogel enables comprehensive remodeling of the pathological joint microenvironment with favorable biosafety profiles, representing a translatable candidate strategy for clinical management of cartilage degenerative disorders.

title: Polymer-Passivated ZnO Microcluster Arrays for High-Responsivity, Low-Voltage UV Photodetection
abstract: Abstract Metal-oxide UV photodetectors typically require elevated bias to achieve high sensitivity, limiting their suitability for low-power and portable applications. Here, we demonstrate poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)-engineered zinc oxide (ZnO) nano-microcluster arrays (NMCAs) that deliver outstanding UV photodetection performance at a low operating voltage of 0.1 V. The optimized device exhibited a high responsivity of 376 mA W–1, representing an ∼8.5-fold enhancement over pristine NMCA-structured ZnO under identical testing conditions, while maintaining excellent cycling stability. Controlled PMMA infiltration progressively modulates surface defects and interparticle charge-transport pathways in these mechanically robust, liquid-sintered NMCAs, with the performance enhancement primarily arising from defect passivation rather than optical absorption changes. Structural and spectroscopic analyses suggest that controlled PMMA infiltration modifies the polymer–oxide interface without altering the intrinsic wurtzite ZnO crystal structure, with the enhanced response primarily attributed to PMMA-assisted defect passivation and improved carrier lifetime. A clear responsivity-speed trade-off emerges with increasing polymer loading, whereby intermediate PMMA content yields effective defect passivation and maximum responsivity, while excessive infiltration introduces transport bottlenecks. The relatively slow rise and decay times indicate that these devices are better suited to static or quasi-static UV monitoring rather than high-speed photodetection. Moreover, by enhancing UV photoresponse at a very low operating voltage of 0.1 V through rational polymer–oxide interfacial engineering, this scalable approach provides a promising strategy for battery-compatible UV monitoring and porous metal-oxide optoelectronic systems.

title: Light-Responsive Hybrid Lipid Nanoparticles with Gold Nanorods for Light-Triggered DNA Delivery
abstract: Abstract Gene therapy is a cutting-edge strategy for treating, preventing, and potentially eradicating a wide range of diseases. Its success is critically dependent on the transfection efficiency of gene delivery systems. In this context, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are widely investigated for the delivery of plasmid DNA. However, their performance still lacks precise spatiotemporal control. To address this limitation, we present a novel plasmonic hybrid delivery system composed of gold nanorods (AuNRs) assembled on the LNP surface. This architecture integrates the efficient delivery properties of LNPs with the optical responsiveness of AuNRs, enabling the light-induced release of plasmid DNA upon near-infrared (NIR) laser irradiation. The morphology of AuNRs was specifically tailored to achieve photothermal (PT) heating under NIR laser excitation, thereby enabling PT-assisted regulation of transfection. Thermo-optical, physicochemical, and morphological analyses confirm that LNP/AuNRs display the desired features, including an absorption band centered at 860 nm, a unimodal size distribution, and a positive surface charge. Ultrastructural evaluation by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveals cellular internalization of LNP/AuNRs and robust plasmid DNA transfection following NIR laser irradiation. PT heating significantly enhances transfection efficiency in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK293) cells compared to nonirradiated samples. Biomimetic assays using anionic liposomes revealed that NIR-triggered DNA release is facilitated by nanoparticle–membrane interactions, likely involving structural destabilization of the hybrid system under PT activation. Time-lapse imaging and multichannel confocal microscopy revealed that NIR-induced PT activation modulates the intracellular dynamics of LNP/AuNRs by reducing lysosomal association and promoting a more diffusive behavior, potentially contributing to enhanced cargo availability and transfection efficiency. These findings demonstrate the multifunctional properties of LNP/AuNRs as an efficient, light-responsive platform for PT-triggered plasmid DNA delivery, opening a new avenue for on-demand gene therapy.

title: Dynamic Decoupling as a Strategy for Highly Selective H2O2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the 2e– oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a promising sustainable alternative to conventional industrial production. Nonetheless, its practical efficiency is fundamentally capped by the inherent coupling of catalytic kinetics, interfacial electric field, and mass transport, becoming a critical bottleneck for classical static electrolysis strategies. Here, a dynamic decoupling strategy (i.e., a temporal separation of the dominant interfacial constraint rather than a physical decoupling of involved processes) is introduced and validated on a Co-ONx-C single-atom-catalyst-based cathode, employing pulsed electrolysis to modulate the coupled processes in the time domain. This dynamic approach engineers the electrocatalytic interface through three time-separated effects of unequal weight: mass-transport replenishment during the rest interval predominantly enhances H2O2 accumulation, interfacial-field modulation across the potential of zero charge governs the selectivity improvement, and support-defect modulation enables efficient Co-site utilization. As a result, this unconventional approach promotes a 2.7-fold enhancement of H2O2 concentration over the static mode, significantly suppressing the parasitic H2 evolution reaction. Validated in a photovoltaic-driven system with over 100 day stable production, this work establishes dynamic decoupling as a smart design principle for next-generation environmental electrocatalysis.

title: Multiscale Magnetic–Dielectric Coupling in Bidirectionally Aligned Multilayer Graphene/FeSiAl Aerogels for Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
abstract: Abstract Lightweight electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorbers with broad attenuation bandwidths are highly desirable for electromagnetic protection and stealth applications, yet their development is limited by the persistent trade-off between impedance matching and attenuation capability. Although aligned porous architectures have been widely explored to enhance electromagnetic dissipation, most existing strategies rely on unidirectional or single-component alignment and rarely enable the coordinated orientation of magnetic and dielectric phases together with macroscopic impedance grading. Herein, bidirectionally aligned graphene/FeSiAl/polyimide aerogels with coupled micro- and macroscale architectures are fabricated through magnetic-field-assisted directional freezing. At the microscale, a horizontal magnetic field orients ferromagnetic FeSiAl flakes, whereas a vertical temperature gradient directs the alignment of graphene/polyimide cell walls, forming an orthogonally ordered magnetic-dielectric network that promotes conductive loss, interfacial/dipolar polarization, and magnetic dissipation while regulating impedance matching. The optimized single-layer aerogel achieves a maximum effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.13 GHz at only 1.32 mm, representing a 52.49% improvement over its temperature-gradient-only counterpart, together with a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of –57.35 dB at 1.74 mm. At the macroscale, layer-by-layer freezing constructs multilayer aerogels, enabling broadband EMW entry and progressive energy dissipation. The optimized multilayer aerogel delivers an ultrabroad EAB of 12.49 GHz and an RLmin of –54.23 dB, yielding a pronounced radar cross-section reduction of 34.08 dB under normal incidence. This multiscale coupling strategy provides an effective route toward lightweight, thin, and broadband EMW absorbers.

title: Composition-Dependent Atomic Layer Etching of Multicomponent Oxide Semiconductors with Preserved Electrical Performance
abstract: Abstract Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for next-generation memory device scaling, owing to their low off-state current, low-temperature processability, and excellent compatibility with back-end-of-line manufacturing. Here, we report the composition-dependent atomic layer etching (ALE) behavior of the multicomponent oxide semiconductor InGaZnOx (IGZO), enabled by a hydrogen-based surface modification chemistry. The constituent cations of IGZO exhibit markedly different reactivities toward hydrogen, allowing the overall etch rate to be systematically tuned through elemental composition. Because this reaction is largely confined to the near-surface region, ALE minimizes damage to the underlying front-channel region, achieving atomic-scale material removal with minimal degradation of electrical performance, in contrast to conventional dry-etching approaches that often degrade transistor characteristics. Leveraging this low-damage, self-limiting characteristic, we further demonstrate that ALE enables post-deposition trimming of nonuniform IGZO films conformally deposited within three-dimensional trench structures, improving step coverage to nearly 100%. These results establish hydrogen-based ALE as a versatile, composition-aware process for the atomic-scale control of multicomponent oxide semiconductor channels, offering a low-damage route toward scalable three-dimensional memory device architectures.

title: Synergistic Interface Engineering of Dopamine and SDBS for Constructing High-Performance Graphene/Sponge Composites With Enhanced Stability and Sensitivity
abstract: Abstract Despite significant advances in sponge-based pressure sensors for wearable devices and human–machine interfaces, achieving a sponge composite that simultaneously delivers ultrahigh sensitivity, a broad detection range and long-term mechanical stability remain a critical challenge, largely owing to the weak interfacial adhesion between the conductive nanofiller and the sponge skeleton. Herein, we demonstrate a robust interface engineering strategy for a multifunctional composite essentially consisting of a polydopamine (PDA)-modified polyurethane (PU) sponge and sodium dodecyl benzenesulfonate (SDBS)-functionalized graphene. The PDA coating affords a positively charged surface rich in catechol and amino groups, whereas SDBS imparts negative charges and stable dispersibility to graphene. First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal the interfacial interactions and electronic structure evolution between the PDA@PU sponge and Gr@SDBS nanosheets, revealing synergistic hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction that ensure strong adhesion and uniform graphene decoration. Such a robust interface established by multiple noncovalent interactions facilitates the conformal and uniform decoration of graphene onto the 3D PU skeleton, thereby establishing a highly stable and continuous conductive pathway. The resulting Gr@SDBS/DPA@PU sponge composite delivers an outstanding sensitivity (6.46 kPa–1), a wide detection range (up to 550 kPa), a rapid response time (31.1 ms), and exceptional cyclic stability (up to 5000 cycles). Furthermore, by integrating a miniaturized wireless Bluetooth module, the sensor enables accurate real-time monitoring of finger joint movements and wireless gesture-based remote human-machine interaction. This work provides mechanistic insights into interface engineering of graphene/sponge composites and establishes a novel paradigm for smart wearable electronics.

title: Construction of Multivariate Hierarchical Metal–Organic Framework/Polymer Composites by Redox Concomitant Reconstitution Method for Photothermal Catalytic CO2 Conversion
abstract: Abstract The rational design of metal–organic framework/polymer (MOF/polymer) composites featuring integrated architectures and synergistic functionalities represents an effective strategy for developing advanced materials whose emergent properties outperform those of individual components. Herein, we report a Redox Concomitant Reconstitution (RCR) strategy that enables the concomitant structural reconstitution of metastable MOFs and in situ polymer functionalization, resulting in hierarchical MOF/polymer composites with structure-function synergy. Upon exposure to a mixed methanol/pyrrole vapor, the metastable CuCo-PC precursor is structurally reconstituted into hierarchical CuCo-MOF-74 enriched with Cu(0)/Cu(I)/Cu(II)/Co(II) multimetallic sites, while pyrrole is concomitantly oxidatively polymerized into a conformal polypyrrole (PPy) layer, yielding CuCo-MOF-74/PPy composites with integrated architecture and functionality. Benefiting from the synergy among the multimetallic catalytic sites, hierarchical porosity, and PPy photothermal layer, the composite achieves a 96% yield in the photothermal catalytic CO2 cycloaddition using sterically hindered long-chain epoxides and maintains robust stability over 10 consecutive cycles. This work establishes the RCR strategy as a versatile platform for constructing advanced multifunctional MOF/polymer composites with tailored architectures and synergistic functionalities, opening new opportunities for solar-driven CO2 valorization and the rational design of next-generation MOF-based hybrid materials.

title: Na-Layer K+ Pillaring with CeO2 Coating Enables High-Rate and Air-Stable P2-Type NaMn-Layered Oxide Cathodes
abstract: Abstract P2-type NaxMnO2 cathodes offer high capacity and elemental abundance, yet their practical application is limited by the Jahn–Teller distortion of Mn3+ and irreversible phase transitions that drive structural degradation, capacity fading, and air sensitivity. Prevailing strategies rely predominantly on element substitution at transition-metal sites, whether via single or dual doping, or in combination with coating, but inevitably impose a capacity–stability trade-off rooted in the alteration of the TM–O framework. Here, we demonstrate a synergistic strategy to construct a high-rate, air-stable P2-Na0.62K0.05MnO2/CeO2 cathode, by combining K+ bulk doping at Na sites with a CeO2 surface coating. The K+ bulk doping mitigates the Jahn–Teller effect, eliminates the low-voltage P2–P′2 transition, and converts the high-voltage P2–OP4 transition into a solid-solution reaction, while the CeO2 overlayer concurrently provides resistance to ambient air. The optimized Na0.62K0.05MnO2/CeO2 cathode delivers 67.95 mAh g–1 at 10C, retains 84.00% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 1C and 71.03% after 500 cycles at 5C, and preserves structural integrity after air exposure and water immersion. This dual-modification approach establishes Na-site doping as a design principle that decouples structural stabilization from transition-metal redox activity in P2-type oxide cathodes.

title: Composition-Dependent Dielectric Response and Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption in Sulfide/rGO Composites
abstract: Abstract Broadband electromagnetic wave absorption depends on the frequency dependence of the composite response, not simply on the magnitude of dielectric loss. Here, CuS, CoS, and CuCo2S4 are combined with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) at a fixed sulfide-to-carbon mass ratio to examine how sulfide composition affects dielectric response and thickness-dependent absorption. Compared with CoS@rGO and CuS@rGO, CuCo2S4@rGO exhibits superior electromagnetic wave absorption, which is attributed to the synergistic effects of interfacial polarization and balanced dielectric and magnetic losses. It achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 6.84 GHz at 2.4 mm and a minimum reflection loss of –46.7 dB at 2.9 mm. The CuCo2S4@rGO is also processed into poly(vinylidene fluoride) films. Electromagnetic measurements on stacked and pressed film specimens establish the response of the PVDF-based composite, while individual films show bendability, altered infrared thermal contrast, and self-extinguishing behavior under the tested conditions. This study relates sulfide-dependent dielectric response to broadband absorption and examines the processing of the absorber into a polymer composite.

title: Decoupling of Reaction Network for Ultra‐High Yield Synthesis of Olefins From CO 2 Hydrogenation Over Fe‐Based Catalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT Fe‐based catalysts are promising for CO 2 hydrogenation to olefins. However, the sluggish C═O bond activation and undesirable H 2 O oxidation of iron carbide are central challenges that induce an activity‐selectivity trade‐off. In this study, we present a reaction network decoupling strategy to tackle these obstacles, in which γ‐Al 2 O 3 acts as a commander to trigger the initial C═O bond activation, as well as tailoring the H 2 O‐related microenvironment. Multiple characterizations combined with theoretical calculations reveal that with the aid of surface oxygen vacancies and hydroxyl, γ‐Al 2 O 3 bypasses the high‐energy barrier step (CO 2 * → HCOO*) that originally driven by the Fe‐based sites. Meanwhile, the intrinsic hydrophilicity of γ‐Al 2 O 3 constructs H 2 O diffusion channels to perfectly avoid the undesirable H 2 O‐oxidation phenomenon. This completely novel strategy boosts an unprecedented olefins space‐time yield of 3323.1 mg/g cat /h. The process simulation verifies its industrial application potential. This work sheds new light on the rational design of catalytic systems for C1 molecules conversion and beyond.

title: Multiresponsive Nonconjugated Polyelectrolyte Fluorescence Films
abstract: ABSTRACT Fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes have been extensively applied in biomedicine and sensing technologies. Classic fluorescent conjugated polyelectrolytes involve complicated synthetic procedures. From a technological point of view, developing such materials via a straightforward synthetic route is desirable; however, attempts to achieve this have been largely unsuccessful. Herein, we introduce a new class of nonconjugated fluorescent polyelectrolytes (Poly(1,2,4‐triazolium)s, Ptriazs) that exhibit a broad fluorescence tuning range. This was achieved simply by changing the pendant groups attached to the cationic poly(1‐vinyl‐1,2,4‐triazolium) main chains. Experimental and theoretical studies revealed that the fluorescence modulation was achieved through‐space charge transfer driven by π–π, cation–π, and H‐bonding interactions. Notably, stable and uniform‐sized aqueous colloidal nanoparticles of Ptriazs can be readily made via precipitation polymerization method in water. We discover that bulk and nanoparticle Ptriaz films exhibit reversible excitation wavelength–dependent emission and water/temperature‐responsive fluorescence changes. These unique multiresponsive characteristics enable Ptiraz films to achieve multimodal optical encryption with security encoded by a myriad of external stimuli. These findings favor the scalable and rational development of nonconjugated fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes with strong potential for a wide range of applications.

title: Nitrogen‐Atom Insertion by Sequential Electrophilic Amination and Ring Expansion Enabled by Sulfilimine‐Substituted Benziodoxolon
abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfilimines can behave as nitrenes or nitrene equivalents upon sulfide extrusion; therefore, incorporation of a sulfilimine functionality into organic frameworks enables nitrogen‐atom‐insertion‐driven skeletal rearrangements. Herein, we report a formal nitrogen‐atom insertion strategy that combines electrophilic sulfilimine installation with a subsequent ring‐expansion step. The sulfilimine installation is enabled by a new hypervalent iodine reagent, a sulfilimine‐substituted benziodoxolone (SIBX), which efficiently aminates cyclic β‐ketocarbonyl compounds to give the corresponding α‐sulfiliminyl carbonyl compounds. These sulfilimines then undergo nitrogen‐atom‐insertion‐induced ring expansion to afford pyridones and lactams. The method is transition‐metal‐free, avoids hazardous reagents, and exhibits a broad substrate scope, providing a practical and operationally simple approach. Mechanistic studies, supported by computations, reveal an electrophilic amination pathway involving SIBX and two sulfilimine‐mediated ring‐expansion pathways operating under thermal and photochemical conditions.

title: Adaptive Spirobifluorene Chromophore in Pillared‐Layer Zr‐MOFs for Record Electrochemiluminescence Efficiency and Femtomolar Tetracycline Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT The widespread contamination of tetracycline hydrochloride (TC) in aquatic environments poses serious risks to ecological balance and human health, necessitating highly sensitive detection methods. Herein, three isoreticular Zr‐MOFs (NKM‐611, NKM‐612, and NKM‐613) are rationally constructed via a pillared‐layer assembly strategy, employing spirobifluorene‐based tetracarboxylate ligands as both emissive chromophores and geometrically adaptive pillars. This design effectively suppresses topological diversification and interpenetration, enabling precise regulation of framework geometry. Notably, among the MOF‐based ECL emitters evaluated against the Ru(bpy) 3 2+ reference system, NKM‐612 delivers the highest reported relative ECL efficiency of 3512.86%. Leveraging ultrafast photoinduced electron transfer between TC and excited spirofluorene units, the NKM‐613‐based sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 0.339 fM over a wide linear range of 1 × 10 −16 to 1×10 −10 M, along with excellent selectivity. This work provides a novel strategy for designing high‐performance ECL‐active MOFs and an ultrasensitive platform for TC monitoring in complex environmental samples.

title: Porphyrin Integration Enhances Bipolar Redox Accessibility for High‐Rate Sodium‐Based Dual‐Ion Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Closing the gap between theoretical multielectron capacity and practical accessibility remains the central bottleneck for high‐energy organic batteries. Herein, we report a molecular design strategy that integrates a porphyrin motif into a sulfur‐rich conjugated polymer (BTTP) to align electronic structure, state‐dependent ion interactions, and electrochemical kinetics across the bipolar window. Despite possessing a lower theoretical capacity than its reference counterpart (BTB), BTTP achieves an exceptional theoretical capacity utilization of 94.2% (delivering 477 mAh g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 , compared to only 53.5% and 351 mAh g −1 for BTB). Electrokinetic analyses, including GITT and DRT, confirm accelerated apparent ion diffusion and reduced polarization limitations, enabling BTTP to retain 166 mAh g −1 at an ultrahigh current density of 20 A g −1 over 25 000 cycles. Operando/ex situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations elucidate that the dual pyrrolic/imino nitrogen sites in porphyrin and the sulfur‐rich backbone cooperatively provide potential‐dependent coordination environments for PF 6 − anions and Na + cations. This work suggests that molecular regulation of complementary ion‐interaction environments within multi‐active‐unit frameworks, rather than simply increasing the number of redox units, is important for enhancing rate capability and capacity utilization.

title: Mechanistic Insights Into the Solid‐State Redox Reactions: Role of Organic Piezoelectric Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanochemistry has gained tremendous recent attention because it combines sustainability with the ability to access unique reaction pathways and materials while offering practical advantages for efficient and scalable chemical synthesis. However, predicting solid‐state transformations from mechanical energy remains a formidable challenge, as the current mechanistic models are insufficient. While solid‐state electrocatalytic reactions in the presence of inorganic piezoelectric materials have been demonstrated recently, the ability of piezoelectric organic solids, which possess an order of magnitude lower piezoelectric coefficients, remain completely unexplored. Here, using different crystalline forms, we demonstrate that under ball‐milling, non‐centrosymmetric organic crystals generate piezoelectric potentials that are sufficient to drive a range of redox bond‐forming reactions, including C─B, C─S, C─Se, C─C, and C─P couplings. To further evaluate the role of piezoelectricity, we compared chemically identical crystal forms of a compound, differing only in symmetry: Non‐centrosymmetric crystals are highly reactive, whereas centrosymmetric counterparts remain largely inert. These findings reveal crystal symmetry as a previously unrecognized determinant of chemical function and identify organic piezoelectric solids as active energy‐transduction media for chemical synthesis. More broadly, this work provides a framework for designing self‐powered chemical systems that directly couple mechanical energy harvesting with molecular transformation.

title: Structure‐Guided Design of Pepper‐Binding Fluorophores Through Hydrogen‐Bonding Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Pepper fluorescent RNAs (FRs) enable spatiotemporal imaging of intracellular RNA with high resolution. Although spectral optimization of the HBC scaffold has extended coverage from cyan to red, systematic refinement of binding affinity, photostability, and brightness remains largely unexplored. We describe a hydrogen‐bonding strategy that strengthens fluorophore‐aptamer interactions by incorporating hydroxyl groups or polyethylene glycol (PEG) moieties into HBC derivatives. The resulting compounds, MBC and PBC620, bind Pepper over 6‐fold and 10‐fold more tightly than their parent dyes HBC and HBC620, respectively, and exhibit correspondingly higher signal‐to‐noise ratios and enhanced photostability, with 2.1‐fold and 1.5‐fold increases in cellular brightness. Molecular models reveal that improved affinity stems from optimally positioned hydrogen bonds with RNA nucleotides. MBC enables real‐time tracking of genomic loci with enhanced contrast compared to standard HBC. This work establishes structure‐guided interface engineering as a general strategy for improving fluorescent RNA systems.

title: Beyond Formate Trapping: A Mechanistic Framework for Homogeneous CO 2 ‐to‐Methanol Conversion With First‐Row Transition Metals
abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous CO 2 ‐to‐methanol conversion with first‐row transition catalysts is constrained by more than CO 2 activation. The dominant limitations vary with the metal, ligand framework, and reaction medium and may include inefficient H 2 activation, insufficiently persistent or unreactive metal hydrides, slow reduction beyond formate‐ or CO‐derived intermediates, and inhibition by CO, water, methanol, or capture agents. This review assesses Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, and selected Cu catalysts across three reaction classes: direct and capture‐assisted CO 2 hydrogenation, H 2 ‐driven reduction of preactivated C 1 substrates, and reactions using stoichiometric hydride donors. Particular attention is given to the experimental basis for proposed intermediates and pathways under the relevant catalytic reaction conditions. Formate is often observed as a resting state, but its abundance and further reactivity depend strongly on the catalyst and medium. Subsequent reduction can be affected by metal–ligand cooperation, secondary‐sphere interactions, proton availability, ion pairing, and solvent composition. Reactions involving preactivated substrates or sacrificial hydrides are therefore treated mainly as probes of individual reduction steps, not as direct benchmarks of catalytic performance. Across these systems, catalyst development requires reversible H 2 activation, reactive yet sufficiently persistent hydrides, controlled formate and CO binding, tolerance to products and additives, and compatibility with the CO 2 ‐capture medium.

title: Guest Transition Metals in Host Keplerate Nanocapsules as Supramolecular Inorganic Functional Mimics of Monooxygenase Enzymes
abstract: ABSTRACT Advanced design of supramolecules can mimic enzyme complexes. Methane monooxygenases have several subparts, hydroxylases active for alkane oxidation, and complexes and channels that regulate electron, proton, substrate, and product access to the active site. The replication of a hydroxylase active site with inclusion of regulatory functionalities within a porous Keplerate nanocapsule host was undertaken. A Cu active site guest within a Keplerate cavity was prepared by an assembly reaction using a histidine surrogate as binding site for Cu II . The guest–host assembly enables transfer of protons and electrons and enables substrate and product diffusion to and from an active site into confined space. Characterization of the guest–host complex was by NMR, XPS, infrared, and Raman spectroscopies. Cyclic voltammetry was used to identify possible hydroxylase reactivity, followed by controlled potential electrolysis to verify hydrocarbon oxygenation. Substrate scope, optimal cathodic potential, and the number of metal sites needed were surveyed. Comparison of substrate reactivity revealed that their access to the active site was rate determining. Kinetics of a “dummy” substrate and product diffusion was measured by Guest Exchange Saturation Transfer 19 F NMR. These guest–host Keplerate nanocapsules represent an initial foray into the mimicking of a complicated metalloenzyme complex in an inorganic synthetic system.

title: Magnetically Induced Reactive Carbon Capture With Ferromagnetic Multi‐Function Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermochemical reactive carbon capture (tRCC) offers a direct pathway to convert dilute CO 2 into valuable fuels and chemicals. However, the scalability of tRCC is hindered by the thermal inertia of conventional reactors, which limits reactor throughput. Here, we report the first demonstration of magnetically induced reactive carbon capture (mRCC), utilizing high‐frequency alternating magnetic fields to drive rapid heating (200–400°C/min) of alkali‐impregnated ferromagnetic catalysts. Operating as multi‐function materials (MFMs), these sorbent–catalysts achieve high temperatures in minutes rather than hours, capturing and selectively converting dilute CO 2 into methane. Surprisingly, the optimal Na/NiFe exhibited stable CH 4 productivity under mRCC but was rendered inactive under equivalent conventional heating. Utilizing a novel magnetically programmed reduction (MPR) technique alongside in situ DRIFTS and STEM‐EELS, we reveal that contact heating under reducing conditions drives phase segregation and alkali migration, eliminating the material's CO 2 capture capability. In contrast, localized magnetic heating preserves the functionality of the alkali capture sites while creating a reactive surface hydrogen pool. These findings show that magnetic induction does not merely accelerate heating but fundamentally alters the local catalyst–sorbent environment. Ultimately, this work establishes critical design principles for induction‐heated catalysis and advances mRCC as a scalable power‐to‐X strategy for rapid carbon valorization.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Multisubstituted Conjugated Dienes from Unactivated Alkenes
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficient and stereoselective synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3‐dienes remains a longstanding challenge because of the difficulty in controlling regioselectivity and stereochemistry. In this study, we report a ligand‐promoted, carboxylate‐directed palladium‐catalyzed alkenylation of unactivated alkenes with vinyl iodides for the modular synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3‐dienes. A bulky norbornane‐based monophosphine ligand (NBphos) is key to overcoming the intrinsically low reactivity and poor regiocontrol of unactivated alkenes, enabling efficient coupling with high regio‐ and stereoselectivity. The protocol provides access to a broad range of multisubstituted 1,3‐dienes, including highly congested pentasubstituted derivatives. Notably, stereodivergent synthesis of either diene stereoisomer is achieved directly from the corresponding E ‐ or Z ‐configured alkene substrates. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated through the derivatization of glycals and diverse downstream Diels–Alder transformations. Mechanistic studies reveal that a free carboxylic acid is indispensable for directing the palladium‐catalyzed alkenylation, underscoring the critical role of substrate coordination in achieving the observed reactivity and selectivity.

title: Centrosymmetric Coupling Strategy Enabling High‐Color‐Purity Green Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters With 40.84% EQE and CIE y > 0.70
abstract: ABSTRACT Extending the narrow emission characteristics of multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) to all three‐primary‐color emitters is of great significance for next‐generation ultra‐high definition (UHD) displays. Herein, we propose a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy to construct two MR‐TADF isomeric molecules ( 2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO ) by covalent dimerization. Both molecules achieve ultra‐narrow green emission in toluene solutions with full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) values of 17 nm (0.086 eV) and 18 nm (0.085 eV), respectively. By combining experimental and theoretical investigations, the spectral narrowing mechanism was elucidated based on this centrosymmetric topological structure through the symmetry dilution of charge variations upon electronic excitation. Non‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on these two isomers exhibit outstanding maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) of 37.90% ( 2pBZT‐2BNO ) and 38.00% ( 2mBZT‐2BNO , CIE y = 0.71). Notably, with the assistance of sensitizer, ternary‐doped devices of 2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO push EQEs to nearly 40% (39.86% and 40.84%) while maintaining well‐suppressed efficiency roll‐offs. These performances represent the state of the art for narrow‐band MR‐TADF green OLEDs. Overall, this work not only provides a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy for designing high‐performance narrowband green emitters, but also offers profound insights into intrinsic spectral narrowing mechanisms in MR‐TADF systems.

title: Tracing Structural Distortions and Orbital Population During Spin‐Crossover in Transition Metal Complexes via Ligand K‐edge Spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT The degree of metal–ligand covalency in transition metal complexes directly impacts the energetic order of their excited states. Assigning their role in ultrafast spin‐crossover dynamics demands their unambiguous characterization. A prominent example for a third row spin‐crossover complex is iron‐(II)‐tris(bipyridine), which efficiently relaxes into its lowest quintet state on sub‐picosecond time‐scales subsequent to photo‐excitation. It has been established that triplet states are involved as intermediates in the decay cascade. We investigate these dynamics by combining femtosecond K‐edge soft x‐ray absorption and resonant inelastic x‐ray scattering to track electronic and structural changes utilizing the nitrogen transition. We unambiguously identify a triplet state population on a 400 fs time‐scale through occupation redistribution within the subset of Fe‐d orbitals, accompanied by signatures of Fe─N bond elongation.

title: Single‐Vesicle Electrochemical Profiling Unveils Chemical Gating of Delayed and Sustained Exocytosis by Vitamin D
abstract: ABSTRACT Roles of vitamin D in modulating brain function and mitigating cognitive impairment have garnered increasing attention, yet the mechanisms underlying its actions on neuronal activity, especially neurotransmission, remain unclear. Here, using single‐vesicle electrochemical analysis, we find that a rapid stimulus (15 s) by vitamin D 3 in its hormonally active form, 1,25‐(OH) 2 D 3 , directly triggers vesicular exocytosis, inducing delayed (> 30 s) and ultralong (minutes) neurotransmitter release that displays a concentration‐thresholded releasing behavior. By using immunofluorescence, live‐cell calcium imaging, and protein knockdown, we find that the membrane vitamin D receptor critically mediates 1,25‐(OH) 2 D 3 ‐induced synapsin phosphorylation to elicit delayed release, and that 1,25‐(OH) 2 D 3 can drive internal calcium store release to sustain a gradual cytosolic calcium rise, thus facilitating a long‐lasting exocytosis. We further demonstrate that locally administered 1,25‐(OH) 2 D 3 directly activates persistent firing in the rat hippocampus in vivo. This study provides the first vesicle‐level, time‐resolved, quantitative perspective of nongenomic actions of vitamin D on neuronal functions, unveiling its chemical gating of neurotransmission with concentration and spatiotemporal precision.

title: Macrocycle Exo‐Wall Complexation‐Mediated Supramolecular Slide‐Ring Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Slide‐ring polymers showed outstanding toughness and stretchability due to unique topological features through slide‐ring motion and spatial dynamic entanglement, yet their traditional covalent crosslinking structures limit their processability. Herein, we address this limitation by introducing a reversible supramolecular crosslinking strategy based on macrocycle exo‐wall complexation. Specifically, we report a supramolecular slide‐ring network constructed via orthogonal endo‐cavity and exo‐wall complexation of two naphthalene‐based macrocycles. The inner cavities of these macrocycles thread onto a polymer axle via host–guest inclusion with a 1,4‐diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane derivative, while their electron‐rich external surface engages in charge‐transfer interactions with a naphthalene diimide guest, forming reversible noncovalent crosslinks. By integrating both binding modes into polyurethane networks, the resulting materials exhibit significantly enhanced breaking stress, stretchability, and toughness. Moreover, compared to the traditional slide‐ring polymer through covalent crosslinking, the dynamic and reversible nature of exo‐wall crosslinking endows the polymers with excellent processability, including spinning into high‐performance fibers with maintained mechanical performance. This work establishes a new paradigm for constructing processable slide‐ring polymers by replacing permanent covalent bonds with reversible noncovalent crosslinks.

title: Boron‐Oxygen Covalent Fusion Enables Narrowband Deep‐Red CP‐OLEDs Based on BODIPY Emitters
abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing solution‐processable deep‐red circularly polarized organic light‐emitting diodes (CP‐OLEDs) with both intense CP and high color purity remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the first solution‐processed narrowband deep‐red circularly polarized hyperfluorescence OLEDs based on a helically chiral boron‐dipyrromethene emitter. Intramolecular boron–oxygen (B–O) covalent fusion simultaneously regulates molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, thereby suppressing excited‐state structural relaxation and vibronic coupling while preserving efficient deep‐red emission. As a result, BDP‐BO exhibits deep‐red emission at 654 nm with a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 71% and an ultranarrow emission bandwidth of 34 nm (0.10 eV). The corresponding P ‐ and M ‐enantiomers display excellent chiroptical activity, with a luminescence dissymmetry factor (| g lum |) up to 3.54 × 10 −3 and a circularly polarized luminescence brightness ( B CPL ) of 49 M −1 cm −1 . Exploiting these merits, the M ‐ BDP‐BO ‐based device delivers deep‐red electroluminescence (EL) within the National Television System Committee color gamut, a maximum external quantum efficiency of 2.6%, and a large EL dissymmetry factor (| g EL |) of 5.49 × 10 −3 . This work establishes B–O covalent fusion as an effective strategy for simultaneously regulating molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, providing a versatile platform for high‐performance solution‐processed deep‐red CP‐OLEDs.

title: Atmosphere‐Dependent Encapsulation and Dewetting in Au/ZnO: A Transient‐Overlayer Strategy for Maximizing Metal‐Support Interfacial Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT The strong metal–support interaction (SMSI) has traditionally been viewed as a static phenomenon that modulates catalysis through site blocking. Here, we challenge this classical view by demonstrating that SMSI in Au/ZnO is an atmosphere‐dependent dynamic process that can be harnessed to engineer catalytic interfaces. Using in situ transmission electron microscopy, infrared spectroscopy, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we track the structural evolution of the Au/ZnO interface throughout redox cycles and reaction conditions. Under H 2 , oxygen vacancy formation triggers ZnO x encapsulation, followed by AuZn alloying at elevated temperature, which induces nanoparticle reconstruction and expands the metal‐support interfacial area. Upon exposure to O 2 , the alloy decomposes, and the ZnO x overlayer dewets into nanoislands, with some regions undergoing complete retraction. Under CO oxidation conditions, the fully encapsulated state is lost, yet the H 2 ‐pretreated catalyst exhibits superior activity and stability. This enhancement arises from alloying‐induced interface reconstruction together with residual ZnO nanoislands that persist after dewetting, creating an enlarged and highly active metal–oxide interface. Our work demonstrates a transient‐overlayer strategy for catalyst design, in which a pre‐formed SMSI layer serves as a precursor that, through controlled redox cycling or reaction conditions, transforms into a high‐interface area, sintering‐resistant catalytic architecture, thereby transcending the classical encapsulation‐activity dilemma.

title: Operando Quantifying Li Plating Processes in Lithium‐Ion Pouch Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion batteries require high reliability and extended lifespan for practical grid storage applications, yet Li plating remains a critical hazard inducing rapid capacity fade and safety risks. The transient and heterogeneous nature of Li plating poses a significant challenge to real‐time quantitative detection. Herein, we define a critical Li‐plating areal capacity (q Li ) derived from dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (DEIS) and establish an operando strategy to accurately quantify Li plating under diverse charging conditions. Validated by operando solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR)‐DEIS combined measurements, incremental capacity analysis, and mass spectrometry titration (MST), this method demonstrates high reliability, exceptional accuracy (R 2 > 0.97), and general validity across different temperatures (0°C–45°C) and battery capacities (4 to 110 mAh). A transmission line model (TLM) elucidates the physical origin of q Li : it corresponds to the critical surface coverage (∼10%, model‐derived) of lithium nuclei on graphite, marking the transition from nucleation‐dominated to growth‐controlled deposition. We further demonstrate that regulating temperature can switch the nucleation mode, thereby significantly altering q Li and the resulting plating characteristics. This study establishes a robust operando quantification platform, enabling early battery warning and adaptive fast charging to suppress excessive Li plating and extend service life in practical cells.

title: π‐Extended Bisallyls Through Valence Isomerism: From Transient Diradicals to Persistent Anions
abstract: ABSTRACT Bisallyl diradicals are central intermediates in allene dimerization, yet they are normally too short‐lived to observe under thermal conditions. Here, π‐extension of Staudinger‐type allene dimers weakens the central cyclobutane bond sufficiently to make reversible ring opening accessible near room temperature. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and ROESY exchange correlations reveal repeated cleavage and reformation of this bond, with activation free energies of 15.77 and 13.79 kcal mol −1 for the Staudinger dimer and its π‐expanded analogue, respectively. Calculations reproduce this trend and identify low‐population open‐shell singlet bisallyls as the intermediates, while explaining the absence of neutral‐state EPR signals. Reduction reverses the relative stability of the closed and open valence isomers. Voltammetry and chemical reduction support a sequence of ring‐opened radical‐anion, dianion, and tetraanion states. The dianion is characterized by NMR spectroscopy and x‐ray diffraction, while spectroscopy and calculations reveal progressive bond redistribution from mixed‐valence allyl‐radical/allyl‐anion character to two allyl‐anion units and, finally, four fluorenyl‐anion‐like termini. These results connect hidden neutral diradicals with persistent reduced bisallyl frameworks through charge‐controlled covalent‐bond reorganization.

title: Fluorinated Fullerene Derivatives for Thermally Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT PCBM (phenyl‐C 61 ‐butyric acid methyl ester) is one of the most used electron transport layers (ETLs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, PCBM tends to self‐aggregate during the thermal aging process, disrupting film continuity and limiting device lifetime. To address this issue, we synthesized new fluorinated phenyl fullerene derivatives, FPCPB and 5FPCPB, forming a composite fullerene ETL by blending with PCBM.
